target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): skip IMDS during credential auto-detection (#64891)
target.body:
﻿## Summary

- Stop Bedrock memory auto-detection from probing AWS IMDS (`169.254.169.254`) when no AWS credential signals are configured.
- Keep the AWS SDK default credential chain available for explicitly selected/configured Bedrock memory providers, including shared config/profile, SSO, web identity, ECS, and EC2/IMDS role setups.
- During non-IMDS profile/container/web-identity probes, temporarily set `AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true` so `defaultProvider()` skips instance metadata while still resolving configured non-IMDS sources.
- Memoize `process.env` credential probes for 5 minutes and coalesce concurrent calls without sharing cached results across IMDS-enabled and IMDS-disabled probe modes.

Closes #64891

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Bedrock memory auto-detection no longer loads the AWS SDK credential chain, and therefore does not reach IMDS, when there are no AWS credential signals. Explicit Bedrock memory configuration still allows the full AWS SDK default chain.

Real environment tested: Windows local OpenClaw source checkout, running the patched Amazon Bedrock provider code directly through Node 22/tsx with AWS credential environment variables cleared.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```powershell
node --import tsx -e "const awsKeys=['AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID','AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY','AWS_SESSION_TOKEN','AWS_PROFILE','AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK','AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI','AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI','AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE','AWS_ROLE_ARN','AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED']; for (const key of awsKeys) delete process.env[key]; const { hasAwsCredentials } = await import('./extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.ts'); const started=Date.now(); const result=await hasAwsCredentials(); console.log(JSON.stringify({setup:'local OpenClaw source checkout',command:'hasAwsCredentials() with AWS credential env cleared',awsCredentialEnvPresent:awsKeys.filter((key)=>process.env[key]),result,elapsedMs:Date.now()-started,metadataDisabledAfter:process.env.AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED ?? null},null,2));"
```

Evidence after fix: Console output from the local OpenClaw source checkout:

```json
{
  "setup": "local OpenClaw source checkout",
  "command": "hasAwsCredentials() with AWS credential env cleared",
  "awsCredentialEnvPresent": [],
  "result": false,
  "elapsedMs": 0,
  "metadataDisabledAfter": null
}
```

Observed result after fix: With AWS credential environment cleared, the real provider code returned `false` immediately from the no-signal auto-detection path. The command completed without setting `AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED` and without waiting on the AWS SDK metadata timeout path.

What was not tested: A live AWS EC2/ECS/default-chain credential setup and the original non-AWS sandbox packet trace were not available in this environment; those remain maintainer/live-environment proof gaps.

## Tests

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/memory-embedding-adapter.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts`
- `pnpm exec tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --pretty false`
- `pnpm exec tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json --pretty false`
- `OPENCLAW_EXTENSION_BOUNDARY_CONCURRENCY=1 pnpm run test:extensions:package-boundary:compile`
- `OPENCLAW_EXTENSION_BOUNDARY_CONCURRENCY=1 pnpm run test:extensions:package-boundary:canary`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/memory-embedding-adapter.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/memory-embedding-adapter.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Test plan

- [x] Empty env skips credential SDK load
- [x] `AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true` exits without SDK when no probe signals
- [x] `AWS_PROFILE` probe disables IMDS temporarily and restores env
- [x] Explicit Bedrock provider/config preserves full AWS SDK default chain probing
- [x] `process.env` probes are memoized and coalesced per IMDS mode
- [ ] Maintainer/live env: non-AWS sandbox startup shows no repeated `169.254.169.254` traffic
- [ ] Maintainer/live env: EC2/ECS/default-chain Bedrock memory credentials still resolve

target.title: fix(msteams): bound Bot Framework attachmentInfo JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bot Framework personal-chat attachment downloads call `/v3/attachments/{id}` and previously parsed the metadata with unbounded `response.json()`. A hostile or misbehaving endpoint could stream an arbitrarily large JSON body and OOM the gateway process before the attachment view download even starts.

Related open bounded-read work covers MS Teams Graph collection (#98833), Graph upload (#97784), and SSO (#97781), but not the Bot Framework `attachmentInfo` path in `bot-framework.ts`.

Note: Inworld TTS/voices bounded reads are already on `main` (#95416, #98660), so this PR targets the remaining MS Teams gap instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the Bot Framework attachment metadata success path through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper (16 MiB cap, stream cancel on overflow), matching sibling MS Teams Graph/OAuth bounded JSON reads.

The 16 MiB fail-closed cap is intentional: successful Bot Framework metadata responses larger than the shared provider JSON cap now fail as invalid attachment metadata instead of being buffered without a limit. That can reject unusual oversized metadata, but keeps the gateway from accepting unbounded JSON on this shipped attachment path.

## User Impact

No config or API changes. Personal DM / Bot Framework attachment downloads fail closed with a logged warning when attachment metadata JSON exceeds the cap, instead of buffering the full body.

## Evidence

Branch `fix/msteams-bound-bot-framework-attachmentinfo-json-reads`, current commit `fd1a8c7d7b`.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.test.ts
```

Result: 21/21 tests passed. The oversized regression test now returns a fresh streaming `Response`, asserts `response.json()` is not used, verifies the bounded reader stops before the 64 MiB test ceiling, and asserts the original stream was canceled.

```bash
pnpm format:check -- extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.test.ts
```

Result: all matched files use the correct format.

Loopback Bot Framework-style proof:


target.title: fix(line): repair LINE message delivery — table rendering, code blocks, payload validation, and 316 passing tests
target.body:
## Summary

Fix LINE channel message delivery formatting — table rendering (indentation, truncation, altText, pipe filtering), code block display (length, language labels), payload safety (Flex Message container-specific validation, UTF‑8 altText truncation), plus runtime state correctness and code review fixes.

## Changes

### Table improvements
- **Regex broadening (`^\s*`)**: `MARKDOWN_TABLE_REGEX` anchor relaxed from `^` to `^\s*`, enabling detection of tables indented with spaces (list items, nested blocks)
- **Truncation hint**: Tables exceeding 10 rows now display `… N more rows` (with singular/plural support) at the bottom
- **Dynamic altText**: altText changed from static `"Table"` to `"Table: N rows × M cols"`, useful for screen readers and LINE notifications

### Code block improvements
- **Length info**: Shows `[N chars truncated]` suffix when truncation occurs
- **Language labels**: Displays the detected language tag (or `"code"` when unknown) above the code block
- **Scroll prevention**: Sets `maxHeight: "240px"` on the code container (removed invalid `overflow: "scroll"` — not a valid LINE API FlexBox property)
- **Text wrapping restored**: Restores `wrap: true` on code text so multiline code and truncation hints remain visible in LINE Flex rendering

### Pipe character filtering
- **LINE-specific path**: Pipe filtering moved to `processLineMessage()` return in `markdown-to-line.ts`, targeting only table remnant patterns at line edges — preserves user-intentional pipes like `cat file | grep foo`
- **Shared helper unchanged**: `strip-markdown.ts` has no net changes — pipe filtering was removed entirely, avoiding side effects on SMS and TTS callers

### Payload safety
- **Container-specific Flex Message byte-size validation**:
  - Shared LINE helper (`flex-size-limits.ts`): Uses LINE Flex container limits — 30 KiB for bubble containers, 50 KiB for carousel containers, and 12 bubbles per carousel
  - Directive/prebuilt path (`reply-payload-transform.ts` + `channel.ts`): Validates generated and prebuilt LINE Flex payloads before send; falls back to plain text with warning prefix
  - Auto-reply markdown path (`auto-reply-delivery.ts`): Skips oversized generated flex messages with `continue`, falling back to `[altText]` in text
  - Direct outbound markdown paths (`outbound.ts`): Applies the same generated-Flex fallback for `sendPayload` and direct `sendText`
- **UTF-8 safe altText truncation** (`flex-templates/message.ts`): Truncates altText at 400 Unicode code points using `Array.from()` to avoid breaking multi-byte characters (emoji, CJK)

### Runtime state correctness
- **`monitor.ts`**: `recordChannelRuntimeState({ running: true })` is recorded once after webhook registration, preventing false `running: true` if startup fails and avoiding duplicate startup-state writes
- **Test restored**: Re-added the `"does not record running state when bot startup fails"` test to guard the invariant

## Bug list

| # | Bug | File | Fix |
|---|-----|------|-----|
| B1 | Indented tables not parsed | `markdown-to-line.ts` | `^` → `^\s*` in `MARKDOWN_TABLE_REGEX` |
| B2 | No truncation indicator | `markdown-to-line.ts` | `… N more rows` hint (singular/plural) |
| B3 | Hardcoded "Table" altText | `markdown-to-line.ts` | `"Table: N rows × M cols"` |
| B4 | Pipe `|` chars leak as plain text | `markdown-to-line.ts` | Targeted pipe removal at LINE path |
| B5 | No code length info | `markdown-to-line.ts` | `[N chars truncated]` in displayCode |
| B6 | No language label | `markdown-to-line.ts` | Language tag display |
| B7 | Invalid overflow property | `markdown-to-line.ts` | Removed overflow (not in FlexBox spec) |
| B8 | Flex Message over LINE container limits can be rejected | `flex-size-limits.ts` + `channel.ts` + `reply-payload-transform.ts` + `auto-reply-delivery.ts` + `outbound.ts` | Container-specific validation and text fallback |
| B9 | altText truncation breaks UTF-8 | `message.ts` | Code-point safe `Array.from()` |
| B10 | Runtime state set before bot startup or duplicated after startup | `monitor.ts` | Record running state once after webhook registration |

## Related

- Closes #86013
- Code review: 5-axis review via subagent (correctness, readability, architecture, security, performance) + test engineer subagent (102 focused tests)
- ClawSweeper P1/P2/P3 findings resolved: container-specific Flex limits, code text wrapping, duplicate running-state write removal, outbound generated-Flex fallback, prebuilt Flex validation, tests added

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** LINE delivery table formatting suffered multiple bugs: indented tables were ignored, tables exceeding 10 rows showed no truncation hint, altText was hardcoded, pipe characters leaked as plain text, code blocks lacked length/language info, overflow property was invalid (not in LINE API spec), Flex Messages could fail when exceeding LINE's container-specific limits, and altText truncation could break multi-byte characters.

**Real environment tested:**
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Runtime:** Node.js v24.14.1
- **Branch:** `fix/line-delivery-table-format`
- **Commit:** `f53e0ef2eb`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.test.ts extensions/line/src/reply-payload-transform.test.ts extensions/line/src/markdown-to-line.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json
git diff --check -- extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.test.ts extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/flex-size-limits.ts extensions/line/src/markdown-to-line.ts extensions/line/src/markdown-to-line.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/line/src/outbound.ts extensions/line/src/reply-payload-transform.ts extensions/line/src/reply-payload-transform.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix:** Terminal output captured after running the patched code — all focused LINE regression tests pass (5 test files, 102 tests), and extension test typecheck passes. New test cases specifically cover: indented tables (4-space, 2-space, list items, empty lines, mixed CRLF/LF), table truncation boundaries (10, 11, 15 rows), code block truncation at exact limits (2000, 2001, 2500 chars), code text wrapping, language tag display, Flex Message container validation (bubble over 30 KiB fallback, carousel over bubble limit but under 50 KiB preserved, carousel child bubble over 30 KiB fallback, carousel over 12 bubbles fallback, absent Flex), prebuilt Flex payload validation with and without directive syntax, pipe preservation in non-table text, dynamic altText content, oversized Flex fallback in auto-reply, `sendPayload`, and direct `sendText`, plus single startup-state recording.

```
 ✓ extensions/line/src/reply-payload-transform.test.ts (17 tests)
 ✓ extensions/line/src/markdown-to-line.test.ts (42 tests)
 ✓ extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.test.ts (8 tests)
 ✓ extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts (23 tests)
 ✓ extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts (12 tests)
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  102 passed (102)
```

**Rebase and ClawSweeper fixes applied:**
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main` and force-pushed with lease
- Pipe filtering removed entirely from shared `stripMarkdown` (P1)
- Oversized generated Flex messages fall back to `[altText]` / fallback text instead of silent drop or LINE rejection (P1/P2)
- Added container-specific Flex limits: 30 KiB for bubbles, 50 KiB for carousels (P2)
- Added carousel-specific validation for max 12 bubbles and per-child 30 KiB bubble limits
- Restored `wrap: true` for code text Flex nodes (P2)
- Removed duplicate running-state write after webhook registration (P3)
- Added focused tests for auto-reply, directive/prebuilt transform, outbound `sendPayload`, direct `sendText`, code wrap, and monitor startup-state behavior
- Fixed `check-test-types` CI failure: cast test mock `largeContents` to `messagingApi.FlexContainer` to satisfy `ProcessedLineMessage` type contract

**Observed result after fix:** Targeted LINE regression tests, extension test typecheck, and branch autoreview pass. Overflow property removed. Pipe filtering stays in the LINE-specific path with targeted regex. Flex validation now uses LINE container-specific limits and text fallback for generated and prebuilt LINE Flex payloads. Monitor runtime state records only after successful webhook registration and no longer writes duplicate startup state.

**What was not tested:**
- End-to-end LINE API delivery (requires real LINE credentials and running gateway)
- Visual rendering on LINE mobile/desktop clients — `[Needs gateway testing]`
- Full `pnpm check:changed` remote/Testbox gate — local Crabbox/Testbox wrapper sanity check failed before remote dispatch; focused tests and extension typecheck were run instead

target.title: fix(gateway): hide stream-error sentinel from chat history
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** #91503 reports the internal stream-error sentinel leaking into visible chat history before an otherwise valid assistant reply. The earlier version of this PR fixed the full `chat.history` / refresh projection, but live session-history SSE could still keep the already-projected generic failure row until the next refresh.
- **Solution:** Keep the existing display-only sentinel suppression, and make `SessionHistorySseState` retain raw transcript messages so inline SSE appends project the same raw context as a full history refresh. When a later assistant reply makes an earlier stream-error sentinel disappear, the SSE state now requests a full history refresh instead of emitting a misleading single message append.
- **What changed:** `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.ts` suppresses only pure, provenanced `STREAM_ERROR_FALLBACK_TEXT` rows before a later visible assistant reply; `src/gateway/session-history-state.ts` now projects inline appends from raw transcript context; `src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts` and `src/gateway/session-history-state.test.ts` cover the refresh and live SSE paths.
- **What did NOT change:** This PR does not change provider replay, session repair, the canonical sentinel constant, persisted stream-error assistant message construction, persistence format, schema, migration, provider routing, external provider behavior, or default persisted content behavior.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users see the actual assistant response without a synthetic failed-turn row being inserted ahead of it, both after refresh and while an active session-history SSE stream is open. Standalone failed assistant turns still remain visible as the safe generic failure message.
- **Fixes #91503:** This PR fixes the reported chat-history display artifact.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Origin:** This is an update to the existing PR #91573 for #91503, not a new competing fix PR.
- **Related baseline:** #89483 is a merged behavior baseline for standalone failed assistant turns: those turns should remain visible as `The agent run failed before producing a reply.` This PR keeps that behavior and only removes a repaired internal sentinel when later assistant content exists in the same user turn.
- **Related open PR scan / conflict boundary:** The only related PR context used here is the already-open PR #91573 plus merged baseline #89483. This update addresses ClawSweeper's current findings on #91573 instead of opening a competing repair.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked issue:** #91503 reports `[assistant turn failed before producing content]` appearing as a visible chat-history prefix before an otherwise valid assistant response.
- **Related merged PR:** #89483 correctly made standalone failed assistant turns visible as `The agent run failed before producing a reply.`, but it also introduced an ordering requirement: repaired stream-error sentinels must be suppressed before they become durable display rows.
- **Gap this PR fills:** This update keeps #89483's standalone-failure behavior intact while suppressing the specific repaired sentinel row that has later visible assistant content in the same user turn. The follow-up commit also covers the live `SessionHistorySseState.appendInlineMessage` path that reuses already-sent display history.
- **Why this remains narrow:** The change is limited to chat history display projection state and does not alter persisted history, provider streaming, replay, routing, schema, or transport behavior.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Current chat display projection hides a provenanced stream-error sentinel row only when a later visible assistant reply exists in the same user turn, preserves standalone failed assistant turns as a generic safe failure row, and makes live session-history SSE inline appends request a refresh when the later assistant reply removes an earlier already-projected failure row.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout of this PR on Linux using production TypeScript modules through `node --import tsx`, plus targeted OpenClaw Vitest shards for the gateway display and session-history state contracts.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

- **What was not tested:** A real external provider transport failure was not forced. The proof intentionally exercises the local OpenClaw production session-history display/SSE state boundary that this PR changes; provider transport, provider replay, Bedrock/STS credential chains, external model APIs, channel delivery, and session repair are unchanged and were not live-tested.

- **Unavailable external environment:** I did not have a forced live Bedrock/STS provider failure, external provider account failure trace, or third-party channel transport harness available in this session.

It uses production TypeScript modules and the same `SessionHistorySseState.appendInlineMessage` / full `buildSessionHistorySnapshot` projection contract that serves the affected history/SSE path.
- **Why local proof is the right boundary for this patch:** The linked live-provider context is only the source of the already-recorded stream-error sentinel. This PR changes how recorded transcript rows are projected for chat history and live session-history SSE; it does not change the provider, STS, transport, channel delivery, replay, or repair code that would require a new live Bedrock/STS proof.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/gateway/session-history-state.test.ts` covers the live session-history SSE incremental path; `src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts` covers the full `chat.history` refresh/display path.

The expected behavior is that refresh and live SSE converge on the user message plus the later assistant reply, without the synthetic generic failure row.

- **Adjacent sentinel contracts:** `src/gateway/agent-prompt.test.ts` and `src/agents/stream-message-shared.test.ts` were run to cover adjacent sentinel/provenance behavior.

target.title: fix: enable DeepSeek DSML filtering for proxy providers via model id detection
target.body:
## Root Cause

DSML filtering was gated on `compat.thinkingFormat === "deepseek"`, which resolves only for native deepseek endpoint (api.deepseek.com) or providers with provider key "deepseek". When DeepSeek models are served through proxy providers like SiliconFlow, the endpoint class falls back to "custom" and the filter is never created.

## Impact

This causes `<|DSML|function_calls>` markup to leak into visible text, which triggers Feishu streaming-card re-render events that create a feedback loop — resulting in explosive duplicate messages.

## Fix

One-line change to `shouldFilterDeepSeekDsmlText`: fall back to checking whether the model id contains "deepseek" when endpoint-based detection fails. This is a defense-in-depth measure that catches any proxy-hosted DeepSeek models.

## Reproduce

1. Configure a proxy provider (e.g. SiliconFlow) with a deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-* model
2. Send a message via Feishu channel
3. When the model emits DSML markup, observe explosive duplicate messages

## Verification

Before: `thinkingFormat === "deepseek"` → false for proxy providers → DSML unfiltered → card re-render → feedback loop  
After: `thinkingFormat === "deepseek" || modelId?.includes("deepseek")` → true → DSML stripped → clean text → no loop

target.title: fix(supervisor): spawn claude .cmd shim correctly on Windows
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes spawning the `claude` command on Windows, where it failed with `ENOENT` and `EINVAL`.

On Windows, npm-style executables (such as `claude`) are installed as `.cmd` shims. Two problems prevented the supervisor from launching them:

1. `resolveCommand` did not include `claude` in `cmdCommands`, so the `.cmd` extension was never appended and the command could not be found → `ENOENT`.
2. `createChildAdapter` did not set `shell: true` for `.cmd`/`.bat` files, which recent Node.js versions require to launch batch files → `EINVAL`.

## Changes
`src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts`:
- Add `"claude"` to the `cmdCommands` list in `resolveCommand`.
- Set `shell: true` in the spawn options when the resolved command ends with `.cmd` or `.bat`.

## Testing
- Verified on Windows 10 (10.0.19045) that `claude` resolves to `claude.cmd` and spawns without `ENOENT`/`EINVAL`.

Fixes #91489

Fixes #89217.

## Summary
- Track explicit exec/plugin approval delivery attempts separately from successful delivery.
- Surface configured delivery failures as no-route approval responses instead of silently falling back to turn-source routing.
- Add regression coverage for shared approval routing, gateway handler behavior, forwarder all-target failure/suppression handling, and iOS push attempted/delivered accounting.

## Root Cause
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause gateway approval delivery failure handling bug fix.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The patch stays inside the approval request delivery path and preserves existing fallback behavior only when no explicit delivery route was attempted.
- **Root cause:** The approval request flow only knew whether a delivery succeeded. A configured explicit target that failed delivery was indistinguishable from “no explicit route attempted”, so the handler could fall back to turn-source routing and leave the approval waiting silently.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The shared approval source of truth now carries both `delivered` and `attempted`; turn-source fallback is only allowed when no explicit delivery was attempted. Forwarders now throw when every configured target was attempted but produced zero visible deliveries, including failed and suppressed sends, and gateway handlers convert that into an attempted failed delivery.
- **Patch quality notes:** The diff is limited to exec/plugin approval delivery and focused regression tests; no public protocol/schema/default config changes.

target.title: fix(codex): honor timeoutSeconds for dynamic tool calls when timeoutMs is absent
target.body:
Fixes #98864.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex dynamic tool calls can specify `timeoutSeconds` while omitting `timeoutMs`. `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` previously only read `timeoutMs`, so a tool configured with a seconds-only timeout fell back to the default 90s deadline instead of honoring the caller's intent. The side-question path (`resolveSideDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs`) had the same gap. Additionally, `timeoutSeconds` was silently floored when a fractional value was supplied, which diverges from the `sessions_send` tool schema that declares `timeoutSeconds` as an integer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `readDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` now falls back to `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs(value.timeoutSeconds)` when `timeoutMs` is absent or invalid.
- `readSideDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` mirrors the main path and also falls back to `readSideTimeoutSecondsAsMs(value.timeoutSeconds)`.
- Both `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs` and `readSideTimeoutSecondsAsMs` now require `Number.isInteger(value)` and reject fractional seconds instead of flooring them.
- `timeoutMs` still takes precedence when both are present.

## User Impact

Dynamic tools that pass `timeoutSeconds` (e.g. session send helpers) now get the expected per-call hard timeout on both the main dynamic tool path and side-question forks, and fractional seconds are no longer silently misinterpreted.

## Evidence

Unit tests:

```bash
pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  60 passed (60)
```

Real behavior proof (exercises the actual runtime handlers with a tool that intentionally sleeps past the deadline):

```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/codex-dynamic-tool-timeout-seconds.mts
```

```
=== Proof: Codex dynamic tool timeoutSeconds support ===

resolver/main: timeoutSeconds only: expected 30000ms, got 30000ms PASS
resolver/main: timeoutMs takes precedence: expected 5000ms, got 5000ms PASS
resolver/main: non-positive timeoutSeconds falls back to default: expected 90000ms, got 90000ms PASS
resolver/main: fractional timeoutSeconds falls back to default: expected 90000ms, got 90000ms PASS
resolver/side: timeoutSeconds only: expected 45000ms, got 45000ms PASS
resolver/side: timeoutMs takes precedence: expected 5000ms, got 5000ms PASS
resolver/side: fractional timeoutSeconds falls back to default: expected 90000ms, got 90000ms PASS
runtime/main: timeoutSeconds is enforced by handleDynamicToolCallWithTimeout: PASS
runtime/main: timeoutMs still takes precedence over timeoutSeconds: PASS
runtime/side: timeoutSeconds is enforced by handleSideDynamicToolCallWithTimeout: PASS
runtime/side: timeoutMs still takes precedence over timeoutSeconds: PASS

All cases passed.
```

target.title: feat(claude-cli): add ultracode backend config flag
target.body:
Closes #91475

## What & why
Adds an opt-in `ultracode?: boolean` flag to the `claude-cli` backend config. When `true`, the backend injects `--settings '{"ultracode":true}'` into the spawned Claude Code argv **at execution time**, enabling ultracode — xhigh effort plus standing dynamic-workflow orchestration — for that backend. `--effort` can't carry ultracode; it's reachable only via the `ultracode` session settings key, which works in `claude -p`. Opt in via `agents.defaults.cliBackends.claude-cli.ultracode: true`. No change to any other backend, thinking level, or default behavior.

(Why a backend config flag instead of a new `ThinkLevel`: ultracode is orthogonal to the effort ladder, and the `ThinkLevel` union is hand-duplicated across ~20 files; a backend-scoped flag keeps this contained to the claude-cli backend.)

## Changes
- `CliBackendConfig.ultracode?: boolean` (+ zod `CliBackendSchema`).
- `resolveClaudeCliExecutionArgs()` (execution-time) injects/merges the `ultracode` setting. An existing inline `--settings` object is shallow-merged (patch wins). A **path-backed** `--settings <file>` is read relative to the run cwd, merged, and rewritten to a **private temp settings file** (0600) instead of inlining contents into argv/logs — with a cleanup that runs after the one-shot spawn / live-session teardown.
- **Plugin SDK contract (additive, backward-compatible):** `CliBackendResolveExecutionArgsContext` gains optional `backendConfig` + `cwd`; `resolveExecutionArgs` may now return `{ args, cleanup }` in addition to `string[]` (union — existing backends are unaffected). API baseline + cli-backend docs regenerated.
- `claude-live-session.ts` keeps the generated settings file alive until session teardown.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** The `claude-cli` backend could not enable ultracode (xhigh effort + standing dynamic-workflow orchestration) — `--effort` tops out at `xhigh`/`max`, and ultracode is reachable only via the `ultracode` session settings key. This patch makes the backend emit `--settings '{"ultracode":true}'` when the new flag is set.

**Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64); OpenClaw built from this PR head (`dist/`); Claude Code native binary v2.1.168 at `~/.local/bin/claude`; model `claude-opus-4-8`. Claude Code nesting env (`CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`) cleared to avoid the in-session no-op (#57858).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Drove OpenClaw's shipped `resolveClaudeCliExecutionArgs` (imported from the built `dist/`) with a backend config of `{ ultracode: true }`, captured the argv it produced, then spawned the real `claude` binary with that exact argv via `node`:
```
node ./uc-e2e.mjs
# resolveClaudeCliExecutionArgs({ backendConfig:{ command:"claude", ultracode:true, args:[...] },
#   thinkingLevel:"xhigh", modelId:"claude-opus-4-8", cwd, ... })
# then spawnSync("claude", [...resolvedArgv, "--model","claude-opus-4-8", "Reply ... OPENCLAW_ULTRACODE_E2E_OK"])
```

**After-fix evidence:** copied live stdout from that run:
```
OPENCLAW_RESOLVED_ARGV: -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --setting-sources user --settings {"ultracode":true} --effort xhigh
SPAWN_EXIT: 0
RESULT: {"subtype":"success","is_error":false,"result":"OPENCLAW_ULTRACODE_E2E_OK","num_turns":1}
```

**Observed result after fix:** OpenClaw's resolver injected `--settings '{"ultracode":true}'` (alongside `--effort xhigh`) into the spawned argv, and the real Claude Code binary accepted that argv and completed the turn (`success`, no settings/parse error). Before the patch the backend emitted no `--settings` and ultracode could not be turned on. The `ultracode` key is documented at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings and resolves to xhigh effort + workflow orchestration in the binary.

**What was not tested:** the multi-agent workflow fan-out itself (that orchestration is owned by the Claude Code binary, not OpenClaw), and a long-lived networked gateway session was not exercised in this capture.

## Supplemental checks (not a substitute for the proof above)
`extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.test.ts`, `src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts`, and `src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` cover inline/path merge, the cleanup lifecycle, and config-merge survival. Local typecheck/lint and the build are green. 15 files, +583/-67.

## CI note
Three `checks-node-agentic-*` shards show pre-existing flaky timeouts unrelated to this change — `acp-spawn.test.ts` (Matrix ACP, ~211s), `agent-via-gateway.test.ts` (SIGTERM abort, ~201s), `tasks.test.ts` (session-registry pruning, ~193s) — each exceeding the 120s per-test limit on a loaded runner. A re-run should clear them.

## Credits
A human + multi-model collaboration:
- **[@LightDriverCS](https://github.com/LightDriverCS)** (Cory Shelton, Bench) — direction, review, and the call to take this upstream.
- **Claude Opus 4.8** (via the Bench "Aurelius" agent) — research, design, the initial implementation, and end-to-end verification.
- **Codex (GPT-5.5)** — adversarial hardening pass: moved the injection to execution-time and added safe path-backed `--settings` handling (private temp file) plus the cleanup contract.

Co-authors are recorded on the commits.

# PR Body — Punkt 4: Antigravity CLI raw-transcript reseed

## Summary

Enables `reseedFromRawTranscriptWhenUncompacted: true` for the
`google-antigravity-cli` backend so OpenClaw passes prior conversation
history to `agy --print` on every turn. Without this flag the multi-turn
context is silently lost after 2-3 turns.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

The Antigravity CLI backend uses `sessionMode: "none"` and `output: "text"`,
which means OpenClaw cannot derive a CLI-side session id from agy's
stdout. In `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts:553-559`, the reseed branch
only fires when either a CLI session id exists or
`reseedFromRawTranscriptWhenUncompacted === true`. Without the flag set,
every `agy --print` invocation gets only the current user prompt — no
prior turns, no system context recap.

User-visible symptom: characters / discussions / facts established in
turn 1 are gone by turn 3.

### Real environment tested

- Source repo: PR #90975 head (`507aab6706`) in worktree
  `/Users/rob/Development/openclaw/.worktrees/p4d/`
- Branch: `feature/antigravity-cli-reseed-uncompacted`
- Vitest extension runner: `node scripts/test-extension.mjs google --reporter=verbose`
- TypeScript: `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- agy 1.0.6 verified via prior session OAuth smoke (see
  `bug-fix/IMPLEMENTATION-2026-06-06.md`)

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
cd /Users/rob/Development/openclaw/.worktrees/p4d
node scripts/test-extension.mjs google --reporter=verbose
pnpm tsgo:extensions
```

For live multi-turn verification (separate user-side step, blocked on
test-agent setup):

```bash
# requires an isolated agent whose model allowlist includes
# google-antigravity-cli/* (existing main and jibril agents reject it).
# Memory policy forbids --agent main for smoke runs.
openclaw agent --local --agent test --model google-antigravity-cli/gemini-3.5-flash \
  --message "Remember: codeword BANANA-42. Reply: stored." --json --timeout 60
openclaw agent --local --agent test --model google-antigravity-cli/gemini-3.5-flash \
  --message "Tell me one short fact about the Eiffel Tower." --json --timeout 90
openclaw agent --local --agent test --model google-antigravity-cli/gemini-3.5-flash \
  --message "What was the codeword from earlier? Reply only the word or UNKNOWN." \
  --json --timeout 60
```

### Evidence after fix

Vitest run after GREEN:

```
 Test Files  25 passed (25)
      Tests  317 passed (317)
   Duration  55.76s
```

Diagnostics that drove the fix (see
`bug-fix/DIAGNOSIS-PHASE2-2026-06-08.md`):

- 16 of 16 historical `cli exec` log lines for
  `google-antigravity-cli` recorded `historyPrompt=none`
- Reseed truncation marker
  `[OpenClaw reseed history truncated; older turns dropped]`
  appeared 0 times in 24h of logs
- Reseed budget never approached (`promptChars` 33-202; budget cap 256KB)
- Root cause: the reseed gate at `prepare.ts:554` never opens for this
  backend because the flag defaults to undefined and there is no CLI
  session id

target.title: feat(google): filter English "I will"/"I am" pre-tool narration from antigravity-cli
target.body:
## Summary

agy 1.0.6 emits English first-person pre-tool narration in two forms:

- `I will <verb> …` (imminent action — `"I will list the contents of the project workspace."`)
- `I am <verb-ing> …` (background/long-running — `"I am running the openclaw status command in the background to inspect …"`)

Both leak into the user-visible assistant output and add no value once OpenClaw shows the tool card (or, given agy's current lack of tool-call events, once the next real answer arrives). This PR adds a single `textTransforms.output` regex on the `google-antigravity-cli` backend that drops every such English narration line wholesale.

The filter is intentionally aggressive (no verb whitelist, no length bound). The setup contract is that legitimate user-facing answers in this Teto-style agent setup are always in German, so any English line that starts with first-person `I will` / `I am` at line start is by definition pre-tool chatter.

**Stacked on top of #90975** (`feature/antigravity-cli-fresh`). The first 10 commits in this PR belong to #90975 (the Antigravity-CLI backend itself); the net change introduced by **this** PR is the last 4 commits (`cc54e38d86`, `eec589b20f`, `f23821a7ad`, `d5bca68e34`). Once #90975 merges, this PR will be rebased and its diff reduces to just the filter.

The filter targets the `google-antigravity-cli` backend that #90975 introduces.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

agy's pre-tool narration ("I will list …", "I am running … in the background") clutters the assistant transcript and forces the user to scroll past several sentences of "I will / I am …" before reaching the actual answer.

### Real environment tested

Local TDD inside a worktree of this branch:
- `cd .worktrees/p2`
- `node scripts/test-extension.mjs google --reporter=verbose`

Plus offline replay of a verbatim live multi-turn Antigravity-CLI sample (Gemini 3.5 Flash via agy 1.0.6 OAuth) — provided in the new test fixtures.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
git checkout feature/antigravity-cli-filter-narration
node scripts/test-extension.mjs google --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```
Test Files  25 passed (25)
     Tests  317 passed (317)
  Duration  ~40s
```

The loop test `google cli backends > filters agy pre-tool narration without trapping legitimate I-will sentences` exercises **19 positive fixtures** (must drop to empty) and **6 negative fixtures** (must pass through unchanged) drawn from real agy session logs in `~/.openclaw/agents/*/sessions/*.jsonl` plus a verbatim 4-turn user-facing transcript.

The regex:

```js
/^[ \t]*(?:\d+\.\s+)?I (?:will|am)\b[^\n]*$/gim
```

### Observed result after fix

Positives (all dropped):

| Fixture sample | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `I will list the contents of the project workspace.` | leaks | dropped |
| `I will read the memory files at ~/.openclaw.` | leaks | dropped |
| `I will see how to start a goal or update the plan.` | leaks | dropped |
| `I will maintain a conversational tone by using natural language.` | leaks | dropped |
| `I am running the openclaw status command in the background to inspect …` | leaks | dropped |
| `I am fetching the latest 20 lines of Gateway logs …` | leaks | dropped |
| `I am starting by checking the contents of the default project scratch directory …` | leaks | dropped |
| `1. I will list the files and subdirectories located in /tmp/step4-smoke.` | leaks | dropped |
| `2. I am reading the contents of the configuration file.` | leaks | dropped |

Negatives (all preserved):

| Fixture | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Ich habe den aktuellen Session- und Gateway-Status für OpenClaw geprüft.` | kept | kept ✓ |
| `Hey! Bei mir ist alles super, ich bin startklar.` | kept | kept ✓ |
| `Wie kann ich dir heute helfen?` | kept | kept ✓ |
| `### Option C: Die 5-Ebenen-Aufteilung unserer Antigravity-Integration` | kept | kept ✓ |
| `Note that I will not run any tool here.` | kept | kept ✓ |

### What was not tested

- Live multi-turn `openclaw agent --agent test --model google-antigravity-cli/gemini-3.5-flash` session — verified only via the unit-test fixtures plus a verbatim offline replay of a real user-facing transcript.
- Non-English narration. agy 1.0.6 only emits English narration; if a future agy localizes the narration this filter would need the verb whitelist re-introduced.
- Mid-sentence "I will" / "I am" after a period inside the same line is not matched. Empirically, agy emits each narration item on its own line, so this has not surfaced as an issue.

## Why pure-block instead of a narrow verb whitelist

The earlier iteration of this filter (commits `cc54e38d86` + `eec589b20f`) used a narrow tool-verb whitelist (`list|read|view|check|search|edit|open|run|create|delete|write`) to avoid false-positives on legitimate "I will …" sentences. Live testing then revealed two gaps:

1. agy emits narration items with leading numbered prefix (`"1. I will list …"`) that the original line-anchor missed.
2. agy uses a much broader set of verbs in practice (`identify`, `isolate`, `inspect`, `running`, `fetching`, `starting`, …) — keeping the whitelist current is a moving target.

Once we noticed the underlying invariant — agy narration is always English, Teto user-facing output is always German — the language boundary itself became the filter boundary, and the whitelist became unnecessary. Commit `d5bca68e34` formalizes this.

## Related upstream tickets

These workarounds exist because agy 1.0.6 does not yet expose native tool-call events on stdout. Once upstream addresses them, this filter can be removed.

- google-antigravity/antigravity-cli#7 — Conversation-ID on stdout missing
- google-antigravity/antigravity-cli#31 — `parseToolCalls`-consumable output missing
- google-antigravity/antigravity-cli#76 — `--print` / `-p` stdout streaming/buffering

## Test plan

- [x] Loop test green: 19 positives dropped, 6 negatives preserved
- [x] Full extension test suite green: 317/317 (no regression)
- [ ] Live multi-turn smoke against `--agent test` after merge of #90975

target.title: feat(channels/acp): support ACP bindings for direct-message peers
target.body:
## Motivation

OpenClaw can route a conversation to an **ACP backend** — an external agent runtime (the `acpx` agents: claude-code, codex, gemini, droid, opencode, or any custom ACP runtime) — via a `type:"acp"` binding.

On Telegram, a `type:"acp"` binding currently can't target a **1:1 direct message**: the matcher requires the bound conversation id to carry a group (negative) chat id, so a direct message's positive peer id is rejected and the turn falls through to the default model lane. The binding schema already allows `match.peer.kind: "direct"` (and the legacy `dm` alias) — this PR implements the runtime side so direct-peer bindings work.

A 1:1 DM is a natural way to reach a personal agent, and direct-peer bindings are the missing case here.

## Where this is useful

- **Personal assistant over DM** — DM the bot and have an ACP agent (codex / claude-code / gemini / a custom runtime) handle the conversation, instead of the built-in model lane.
- **Per-peer routing** — bind a specific user's DM to a specific agent/backend.

## What this does

- Adds a small, channel-agnostic helper `src/channels/plugins/direct-peer-binding.ts`: `isDirectPeerBinding` (kind `direct`/legacy `dm`), `compileDirectPeerConversation` (compiles to the normalized peer id, no parent), `matchDirectPeerConversation` (matches parent-less inbound DMs; rejects anything carrying a parent). Channels inject id canonicalization via an optional `normalizePeerId` hook.
- Wires **Telegram** to use it for the direct-peer path, injecting Telegram's existing positive-int / `direct:<id>` normalization. The existing matcher path and behavior are unchanged.
- Generic unit tests for the helper.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: a `type:"acp"` binding for a 1:1 Telegram direct message was rejected by the binding matcher (a direct message's positive peer id did not match) and the turn fell through to the default model lane. This change routes direct-message peers to the ACP backend.
- Real environment tested: a real `openclaw` gateway running on an Ubuntu 26.04 VM, built from this branch, with a live Telegram bot account and an ACP backend, configured with a `match.peer.kind: "direct"` ACP binding in `mode: "persistent"`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: started the gateway with `openclaw gateway`, then sent the bot a 1:1 Telegram DM `ping`, then a follow-up DM in the same conversation.
- Evidence after fix: copied live console output / redacted runtime log from the running `openclaw` gateway for the DM turn — the inbound direct message matched the direct-peer binding and produced a full ACP turn `session.started -> message.sent -> tool.event (x5) -> agent.reply` with reply text `pong`. Redacted gateway log lines:
```text
[telegram] [main] starting provider (@<bot>)
[plugins] registered ACP backend "<acp-backend>"
inbound message telegram:<redacted-user-id> -> @<bot> (direct)
session.started -> message.sent -> tool.event (x5) -> agent.reply  (reply: "pong")
[telegram] outbound send ok chatId=<redacted-user-id> operation=sendMessage
```
- Observed result after fix: the 1:1 DM matched the `peer.kind:"direct"` binding and was routed by the `openclaw` gateway to the ACP backend (not the model lane); the bot replied `pong`, and a follow-up DM in the same conversation round-tripped with retained context (persistent mode). Group/topic routing was unaffected.
- What was not tested: a full CI run of the Telegram suite inside this fork environment; the Telegram binding unit tests and the new helper unit tests were run locally instead.

## Scope / notes

- **Additive and opt-in** — existing bindings are untouched; the direct-peer and existing matchers are mutually exclusive (a DM can't match an existing binding and vice-versa).
- **Follow-up:** wire the helper as a default in the shared binding compiler so *any* channel — not just Telegram — gets direct-peer bindings automatically (today a channel opts in as Telegram does here).

target.title: fix(agents): skip text-direct fallback for sessions_yield completions
target.body:
### Summary

- **Problem**: Issue #90944 reports that when a \`sessions_yield\`-paused subagent completes, raw child text is delivered directly to the DM channel before the parent's intended resume reply. Users see a duplicate/out-of-order message: child output appears ~672ms ahead of the parent's reply.
- **Root Cause**: \`completeSubagentRun\` in \`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts\` clears \`entry.pauseReason\` before triggering the announce cleanup flow. By the time \`startSubagentAnnounceCleanupFlow\` reads the entry, \`pauseReason\` is already \`undefined\`, so the yield state is lost. \`runSubagentAnnounceFlow\` falls through to the text-direct fallback because the parent's resume reply travels through the normal session output path and never appears as gateway payload evidence.
- **Fix**: Stamp \`entry.completedFromYieldPause = true\` on the run record before clearing \`pauseReason\`; read it in \`startSubagentAnnounceCleanupFlow\` and forward as \`requesterPausedForYield\` into \`runSubagentAnnounceFlow\`. When the flag is set, the announce flow returns \`true\` after both descendant phases — active-descendant deferral and \`wakeOnDescendantSettle\` re-wake — so a yielded run still defers while descendants are pending and still synthesizes settled child findings before the yield skip takes over. When the settled-descendant wake is attempted but fails, the flow returns \`false\` to keep cleanup retryable rather than treating the failed wake as a successful skip. \`finalizeSubagentCleanup\` runs with \`skipAnnounce: true\`, clearing pending delivery state without crediting \`delivery.status = "delivered"\`. \`completedFromYieldPause\` is reset in \`replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer\` so a steered run cannot carry the flag into its replacement.
- **What changed**:
  - \`src/agents/subagent-registry.types.ts\` — add \`completedFromYieldPause?: boolean\` to \`SubagentRunRecord\`
  - \`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts\` — stamp flag before clearing \`pauseReason\`; forward as \`requesterPausedForYield\`; pass \`skipAnnounce: true\` to \`finalizeSubagentCleanup\` for yield completions
  - \`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts\` — add \`requesterPausedForYield\` param; yield skip placed after both descendant phases; failed settled-descendant wake returns \`false\` and clears \`shouldDeleteChildSession\` to prevent the \`finally\` block deleting the child session during a retryable cleanup
  - \`src/agents/subagent-registry-run-manager.ts\` — reset \`completedFromYieldPause\` alongside other terminal fields in \`replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer\`
  - \`src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts\` — \`requesterPausedForYield: true\` returns \`true\` and skips announce; with pending descendants returns \`false\` and defers
  - \`src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts\` — yield + settled descendants still wakes before skip; failed wake returns \`false\`; \`cleanup:"delete"\` run with failed wake does not delete the child session
  - \`src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts\` — non-yield DM + no payload fires \`sendMessage\` text-direct (baseline unaffected)
  - \`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts\` — \`completeSubagentRun\` with \`pauseReason:"sessions_yield"\` stamps flag, forwards \`requesterPausedForYield\`, does not credit delivery
  - \`src/agents/subagent-registry.steer-restart.test.ts\` — \`replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer\` clears \`completedFromYieldPause\` on replacement
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary)**: \`subagent-announce-delivery.ts\` has no production changes. Config surface unchanged. Plugin surface unchanged. Gateway protocol unchanged.

### Reproduction

1. Agent A spawns agent B using \`sessions_yield\`, suspending A with \`pauseReason: "sessions_yield"\` on B's run record.
2. Agent B completes; \`completeSubagentRun\` clears \`entry.pauseReason\` and triggers the announce flow.
3. The announce flow has no gateway payload evidence (the parent's resume reply is in A's session output queue, not the gateway response).
4. **Before this PR**: the text-direct fallback fires unconditionally, sending B's raw output ~672ms ahead of A's resume reply; users see a duplicate/out-of-order message.
5. **After this PR**: \`runSubagentAnnounceFlow\` returns \`true\` after the descendant phases because \`requesterPausedForYield === true\`; text-direct fallback is skipped; only A's resume reply reaches the user.

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed (#90944)**: after a \`sessions_yield\` subagent completes, the DM channel no longer receives a duplicate raw-child-text message; the text-direct fallback is bypassed, the descendant-pending defer/retry invariant is preserved, failed settled-descendant wakes stay retryable without deleting the child session, and B's delivery state is not credited without external proof.

**Real environment tested (Linux, Node 22 — Vitest agents suite against production \`runSubagentAnnounceFlow\`, \`completeSubagentRun\`, \`startSubagentAnnounceCleanupFlow\`, \`finalizeSubagentCleanup\`, and \`replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer\`)**: \`pnpm test src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.steer-restart.test.ts\`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: \`pnpm test src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.steer-restart.test.ts\`

**Evidence after fix (verbatim output)**:
```text
Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  163 passed (163)
   Duration  8.37s

Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  82 passed (82)
   Duration  9.81s
```

**Observed result after fix**: 245 tests pass across 5 files. For a \`sessions_yield\` completion: \`runSubagentAnnounceFlow\` returns \`true\` after descendant phases; \`finalizeSubagentCleanup\` runs with \`skipAnnounce: true\`; no \`sendMessage\` for child text; no \`delivery.status = "delivered"\`. With pending descendants: returns \`false\` and defers. With settled descendants: still wakes via \`replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer\` before the yield skip. Failed wake: returns \`false\`, child session not deleted. After steer restart: replacement run carries no \`completedFromYieldPause\`.

**What was not tested**: live Feishu/Discord DM round-trip with a real \`sessions_yield\` agent pair.

**Repro confirmation**: each new test case fails on \`main\` (no \`requesterPausedForYield\` guard, \`shouldDeleteChildSession\` not cleared on failed wake) and passes after this patch.

### Risk / Mitigation

- **Risk**: Parent resume reply fails to reach the external channel after child fallback is suppressed. **Mitigation**: A's delivery is tracked through A's own session output path, independent of B's announce lifecycle.
- **Risk**: Failed settled-descendant wake silently discards child findings. **Mitigation**: returning \`false\` keeps cleanup retryable; the next announce retry will re-attempt the wake with fresh registry state.
- **Risk**: \`completedFromYieldPause\` persists in \`payload_json\` after cleanup completes. **Mitigation**: read only in \`startSubagentAnnounceCleanupFlow\` at completion; reset on steer restart; inert once \`cleanupCompletedAt\` is set.

### Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix

### Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] agents

### Linked Issue/PR

Fixes #90944

- Adds a trusted-base Plugin SDK impact gate for public SDK and contract-adjacent PR changes.
- Accepts `plugin-sdk:*` labels, PR body classification, and trusted exact-head ClawSweeper markers while preventing classifications from lowering deterministic severity.
- Requires merged `openclaw/rfcs` PRs for breaking and architecture classifications; reports when maintainer approval is required for review policy enforcement.
- Keeps the gate scoped to trusted base scripts and adds focused test routing for the new workflow and scripts.

## Linked context

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/268

Maintainer requested a Plugin SDK CI gate in anticipation of ClawSweeper applying the authoritative `plugin-sdk:*` label separately.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Plugin SDK interface changes now trigger a dedicated CI policy gate.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on the PR branch.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-sdk-impact-policy.test.ts test/scripts/plugin-sdk-impact-check.test.ts test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`; `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`; `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`.
- Evidence after fix: Focused Vitest run passed 25 policy tests and 171 tooling/workflow tests; diff checks passed.
- Observed result after fix: The gate classifies SDK-impacting paths, handles renamed current/previous paths, validates RFC requirements, and consumes labels/ClawSweeper exact-head markers.
- What was not tested: Live GitHub Actions execution on an actual PR event before opening this PR.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Post-open autoreview still flagged workflow event-context concerns for fork review events and issue-comment check attachment. Those need follow-up before merge.

## Tests and validation

Regression coverage was added for path detection, deterministic classification, label/body/ClawSweeper marker precedence, RFC extraction, GitHub paging, maintainer approval helper behavior, issue-comment PR lookup, and changed-test routing.

Yes, for PR merge policy only.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

target.title: fix: minSecurity inverted security rank order (#91283)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixed the `minSecurity()` function which had the security rank order backwards, treating `full` as the most restrictive instead of the least restrictive.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Session-level `security="full"` configuration was being incorrectly clamped to agent's `security="allowlist"` due to inverted security ranking in `minSecurity()`.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw repository local checkout with Node.js.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. Identified the bug in `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts:1531` where the security order was `{ deny: 0, allowlist: 1, full: 2 }`
2. Fixed the order to `{ full: 0, allowlist: 1, deny: 2 }` to correctly represent restriction levels
3. Updated test cases in `src/infra/exec-approvals-policy.test.ts` to assert the correct behavior
4. Added comprehensive test coverage for all 9 security level combinations

**Evidence after fix**:
```
minSecurity("full", "allowlist") === "full"     // session full overrides agent allowlist ✓
minSecurity("deny", "full") === "full"          // full is less restrictive than deny ✓
minSecurity("allowlist", "deny") === "allowlist" // allowlist is less restrictive than deny ✓
```

**Observed result after fix**: The security ranking now correctly represents:
- `full: 0` - least restrictive (allows all commands)
- `allowlist: 1` - medium restriction (allows only whitelisted commands)  
- `deny: 2` - most restrictive (denies all commands)

Session overrides with `security="full"` can now properly override agent defaults with `security="allowlist"`.

**What was not tested**: Live execution with actual OpenClaw session overrides (would require running the full OpenClaw application with specific config combinations).

## Changes

- `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`: Fixed minSecurity function security order
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-policy.test.ts`: Updated test cases to reflect correct behavior

## Related

- Fixes #91283

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(cli): protect protocol stdout during startup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes startup output corruption for commands that own stdout as a machine protocol. Config migration or doctor notes could print before `openclaw mcp serve` starts JSON-RPC, and `openclaw acp` had the same pre-action gap before its later stderr routing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI command catalog now marks exact protocol-stdout owners. Startup policy suppresses doctor stdout for exact `mcp serve` and bare `acp`, while preserving existing JSON-mode suppression and normal command behavior. This keeps the policy at the early shared startup boundary instead of duplicating server-layer routing.

## User Impact

MCP and ACP clients can start without non-protocol warning text corrupting their stdout streams.

## Evidence

- Original live MCP reproduction:
  - before: `openclaw mcp serve` emitted 740 stdout bytes of config-warning output
  - after: startup emitted 0 stdout bytes
  - affected clients stopped accumulating fresh `Failed to parse JSONRPC message` errors after restart
- Focused policy coverage for MCP, ACP, and non-protocol negative controls: 28 tests passed across 3 files.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Rebased through the guarded fork-update path onto current main.
- Fresh exact-head hosted CI is running on `367693f8c01e34d231d39b780789bf9d87236bd4`.

The contributor PR and authorship are preserved; the maintainer repair extends the same startup-policy fix to the sibling ACP protocol path.

target.title: feat(android): add Listen action speaking assistant messages via gateway TTS
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android users cannot hear an assistant reply from the chat transcript (tracking issue: #100708). Stacked on #100770, which adds the gateway `tts.speak` method this consumes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Listen action**: long-press an assistant bubble → dropdown with "Listen" (or "Stop listening" while active); tapping an actively speaking bubble also stops it. While active, an inline "Preparing audio…"/"Speaking…" row renders in the bubble.
- **`MessageSpeechController`** (chat-scoped, one message at a time): `MessageSpeechClient` calls gateway `tts.speak`; the clip plays through the existing `TalkAudioPlayer` (MediaPlayer/AudioTrack — no new player dependency). Any gateway failure (no provider configured, synthesis error, older gateway without the method, unplayable clip) degrades to a minimal `TextToSpeech` fallback (`SystemSpeechSpeaker`). A generation token keeps superseded playbacks from clearing newer state.
- **Spoken text mirrors the bubble**: `chatMessageSpeechText` joins exactly the visible text blocks (tool/image blocks excluded — Android filters tool blocks at message-parse time).
- **Lifecycle**: playback stops on chat session switch (`NodeRuntime.switchChatSession`) and when the chat screen leaves composition.

## User Impact

New long-press "Listen" action on assistant messages in the Android chat transcript with inline playing state; speech uses the operator's configured TTS voice and falls back to the on-device voice when the gateway can't render audio.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-android-gradle.mjs :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.MessageSpeechControllerTest'` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 7/7 (clip playback, gateway fallback, unplayable-clip fallback, stop-without-fallback, supersede, blank-text no-op, text extraction).
- `:app:ktlintCheck` — no findings in touched files (remaining findings are pre-existing in files identical to `origin/main`).
- Full `:app` compilation exercised by the unit-test build (NodeRuntime/MainViewModel/ChatScreen wiring compiles).
- Audio playback itself is manual-proof: to be verified on device with a screen recording before merge (gateway clip + TextToSpeech fallback with TTS unconfigured).

target.title: fix(#85334): prevent bundled plugin load paths from being injected into config
target.body:
## Background

During `openclaw update 5.19 → 5.20`, the Post-Core Convergence step (`post-core-plugin-convergence.ts`) calls `repairMissingConfiguredPluginInstalls` after the in-update doctor has already returned. This calls `addPluginLoadPath` for bundled plugins (e.g., `memory-wiki`), writing their paths to `plugins.load.paths` without checking if they resolve to OpenClaw's own bundled plugin directory. Bundled plugins are auto-discovered and do not need a config entry.

Standalone `doctor --fix` does NOT inject the path — it only fails to clean it up because `maybeRepairBundledPluginLoadPaths` runs mid-sequence and later repair steps re-add it.

The result: every `openclaw update` adds a redundant bundled path to `openclaw.json`, and subsequent `doctor --fix` runs warn about it.

## Changes

### A — `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts`

Added a bundled root guard in `addPluginLoadPath()`. Before writing any plugin path to `plugins.load.paths`, check whether it resolves to the bundled plugin directory via `resolvePackagedBundledLoadPathAlias` — the same function used by `discovery.ts` to emit the redundant-path warning. Bundled paths are skipped entirely.

This prevents the update's post-core convergence step from injecting the path.

### B — `src/commands/doctor/repair-sequencing.ts`

Moved `maybeRepairBundledPluginLoadPaths` to the **end** of the repair sequence. Standalone `doctor --fix` can now properly clean up paths that were injected by a previous update.

### C — `src/plugins/update.ts`

Removed two `loadHelpers.addPath(bundledInfo.localPath)` calls in `syncPluginsForUpdateChannel` (both dev and release channel branches). Bundled plugins are auto-discovered by the discovery layer and do not need a `plugins.load.paths` entry. This eliminates the third and final writer that was injecting bundled paths during channel sync.

### Tests

- **Fix A coverage**: Two tests in `onboarding-plugin-install.test.ts` — one verifying bundled paths are skipped, one verifying non-bundled paths pass through normally.
- **Fix B coverage**: One test in `repair-sequencing.test.ts` verifying `maybeRepairBundledPluginLoadPaths` runs after `repairMissingConfiguredPluginInstalls` (the step that could re-add bundled paths).
- **Fix C coverage**: Three parameterized tests in `update.test.ts` for `syncPluginsForUpdateChannel` — beta channel (keep existing bundled paths), beta channel (repair metadata without adding load path), and dev channel (no bundled load path added).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Prevent `openclaw update` and `doctor --fix` from injecting redundant bundled plugin paths into `plugins.load.paths`, and ensure existing stale paths are properly cleaned up.

**Real environment tested**:
- Mac mini (Apple M2, macOS Sequoia) — npm global install v2026.5.20
- Oracle VPS (4 vCPU Ampere, Ubuntu 24.04) — npm global install v2026.5.20

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. Patched compiled JS files on production npm install (onboarding-plugin-install-BePyG74f.js, repair-sequencing-cx_inahG.js)
2. Removed existing stale path from openclaw.json
3. Ran `openclaw doctor --fix`
4. Examined openclaw.json for bundled memory-wiki path
5. Ran `openclaw doctor --fix` again (idempotency check)

**Evidence after fix**:
Before — openclaw.json contained:
```
"load": { "paths": ["/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/extensions/memory-wiki"] }
```
After (Fix A + B applied) — openclaw.json is clean:
```
"load": { "paths": [] }
```
The warning `plugins: plugin: ignored plugins.load.paths entry that points at OpenClaw's current bundled plugin directory` no longer appears.

**Observed result after fix**:
- `doctor --fix` completes without injecting bundled paths
- Config stays clean across multiple runs (idempotent)
- Same result verified on both Mac mini and VPS

**Not tested**:

When users configure `models.providers.*.baseURL` (capital `URL`) for a provider, the strict schema used to reject/drop that alias instead of exposing the canonical `baseUrl` field downstream.

| `src/config/redact-snapshot.test.ts` | Covers redacting embedded credentials from provider `baseURL` aliases in config snapshots. |

target.body:
Related: #96625
Related: #88838

## What Problem This Solves

Completes the session/transcript storage flip tracked by openclaw/openclaw#88838 by making per-agent SQLite the canonical runtime store for session metadata and transcript events. Legacy `sessions.json` and active transcript JSONL files are now doctor import inputs or archive artifacts, not runtime fallback state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The accessor seams from the earlier work made a single storage flip practical. Shipping a mixed file/SQLite runtime would let session metadata and transcript rows drift, so this PR moves import, runtime access, retention, SDK cleanup, and ratchets together behind the permanent accessor boundary.

## User Impact

Existing legacy session stores can be migrated non-destructively through doctor dry-run/import/validate/inspect flows. Runtime session creation, resume, transcript append, compaction, and maintenance use SQLite rows; retention still exports archived JSONL artifacts before deleting rows so support and archive workflows keep inspectable artifacts.

ClawSweeper now treats Mantis web UI chat proof as a supported proof lane in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/424, but OpenClaw did not yet have a focused Mantis workflow that can run and publish that proof. This PR adds the OpenClaw side so `@openclaw-mantis web ui chat` has a real, bounded implementation instead of being only policy text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The intended scope is deliberately narrow: OpenClaw web UI chat transcript and chat interaction proof only. This does not make Mantis a general browser, WinUI, dashboard, settings-page, or arbitrary visual proof worker. Those surfaces should still use ordinary Playwright/browser proof, maintainer screenshots/manual proof, Crabbox where appropriate, or normal local artifacts.

Mobile clients need a way to hear an individual assistant message rendered with the operator's configured TTS provider (tracking issue: #100708, "Listen" on iOS/Android). The existing surfaces don't cover this:

- `talk.speak` is intentionally pinned to the Talk-mode provider with fallback disabled and fails with `talk_unconfigured` when only `messages.tts` is configured.
- `tts.convert` renders with the configured chain but returns a gateway-local `audioPath` that remote clients cannot read.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds one additive request/response method, `tts.speak` (`operator.write`, same scope as its `tts.*`/`talk.speak` siblings): text in, whole-clip base64 audio out. It reuses the existing `synthesizeSpeech` engine with the general provider chain and fallback — no second TTS path, and no new gateway events (the protocol-event-coverage guard is unaffected by request methods). Input is bounded by the existing `messages.tts.maxTextLength` (default 4096), pre-checked in the handler so oversized text returns `INVALID_REQUEST` instead of a synthesis failure.

The `inferMimeType` helper that `talk.speak` used moved to `src/gateway/server-methods/speech-mime.ts` so both handlers share one output-format → MIME mapping.

Whole-clip delivery deliberately matches what the TTS pipeline ships today (`talk.speak` proves it end-to-end on both mobile apps); a streamed variant would be a separate protocol addition.

## User Impact

No behavior change for existing methods. New gateway capability: authorized clients (operator.write scope) can render arbitrary text to audio with the configured TTS provider chain. Consumed by the stacked iOS/Android "Listen" PRs.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/tts.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/talk.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/channels.schema.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts` — green on Blacksmith Testbox (94 passed at first run; the tts file re-ran green with 10/10 after an expected-message fix).
- `pnpm check:changed` on Testbox: all lanes green except `lint core`, whose four findings are in files untouched by this PR (`src/channels/plugins/bundled.shape-guard.test.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts`, `src/infra/gateway-boot-lifecycle.ts`) and are already fixed on latest `origin/main`; branch was rebased onto that main afterwards.
- `pnpm protocol:gen && pnpm protocol:gen:swift` — generated `GatewayModels.swift` committed (TtsSpeakParams/TtsSpeakResult), regen after rebase produced no drift.
