target.title: feat(message): add universal pagination contract with cursor support for MSTeams
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses #71452 — provides the shared pagination contract and CLI cursor support, and wires MSTeams search, read, list-pins, and channel-list as the first provider implementation.

Previously, `renderPaginationHint` inspected provider-specific raw payload fields (`hasMore`, `nextBatch`, `@odata.nextLink`, `total_results`) with no shared contract. Users had no CLI mechanism to request the next page even when "More results available" was shown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduces a universal cursor-based pagination model across the shared runner, formatter, and CLI layers. Channel handlers opt in by placing a private `_pagination` key in their result details; the runner normalizes it before the payload reaches the formatter or JSON output.

### Architecture

```
CLI --cursor <token>  ->  params.cursor  ->  plugin handler  ->  API
                                                                |
                       result.details._pagination        <------+
                                                                |
                       extractPagination(handled)          ->  result.pagination
                                                                |
                       renderPaginationHint(result.pagination)  ->  hint with --cursor value
                       buildMessageCliJson(result)              ->  { pagination: { hasMore, nextCursor } }
```

### Key decisions

- **Opaque `nextCursor` string**: channels produce whatever token their API uses (nextLink URL, offset number, batch token). The CLI and formatter never parse it.
- **Private `_pagination` key**: zero SDK changes. Channels opt in voluntarily. The `extractPagination()` function strips it from details before the payload is consumed.
- **`--cursor` CLI flag** on `read`, `pins`, `search` — all three wired end-to-end for MSTeams.
- **Cursor URL validation before auth**: `searchMessagesMSTeams` and `listMessagesMSTeams` validate cursor URLs against known Microsoft Graph API origins (`v1.0`, `beta`) **before** resolving any auth token — invalid origins never carry credentials.
- **Legacy fallback**: `renderPayloadPaginationHint` preserves existing payload-based hints for providers not yet migrated. Discord `total_results`-vs-count comparison remains as a three-stage fallback chain.

## User Impact

**MSTeams users** can now paginate all three list-producing actions:

| Action | Cursor support | Mechanism |
|--------|:---:|---|
| `search` | cursor pagination | `searchMessagesMSTeams` via `@odata.nextLink` URL |
| `read` | batch list + cursor | `listMessagesMSTeams` (new) — no `--message-id` = list mode |
| `pins` | cursor pagination | `listPinsMSTeams` exposes `@odata.nextLink` when page limit reached |

### Cursor URL validation (production code path, before auth token)

- Valid origins: `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/...` and `https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/...`
- Invalid origins: anything else — rejected with clear error before any auth token is resolved
- `requireValidCursorOrigin` runs in `searchMessagesMSTeams` and `listMessagesMSTeams` before `resolveGraphToken`, so invalid URLs never carry credentials

target.title: fix(ui): scope sidebar session active state to chat
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The proposed Control UI sidebar behavior should not make a recent session row look selected while the operator is on Overview, Settings, or another non-chat route. A stored active session can still be useful for returning to Chat, but selected row styling outside Chat makes the non-chat page look like it is scoped to that session.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change separates the stored/current session from the visual active state in the sidebar. `AppSidebar` still preserves the current session key for Chat navigation and session actions, but it only applies `sidebar-recent-session--active` when the active route is Chat.

The Overview recent-session card also now renders display names directly after `resolveSessionDisplayName`. That keeps the existing provider-key display-name sanitization, while removing the extra digit blur from ordinary titles such as build numbers or dates.

Related existing PR: #97257 disables the session selection control on non-chat pages. This PR is narrower and only scopes the sidebar row active styling.

## User Impact

On non-chat routes, recent sessions remain visible and clickable, but none of them appear selected. Returning to Chat still restores/highlights the stored session, including direct `/chat` and `/chat?session=...` navigation.

Overview recent sessions show non-sensitive numeric suffixes normally instead of blurring them.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/overview/view.render.test.ts`

target.title: fix(ui): turn large pasted text into compact composer attachments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users pasting large plain-text blocks into the Control UI chat composer would dump the entire block into the textarea, making the composer hard to scan and easy to send accidentally.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change treats plain-text paste payloads over 2000 characters as existing composer attachments with `text/plain` file payloads instead of introducing a separate composer-only state model. That keeps send, queue, retry, payload snapshotting, removal, and cleanup on the existing attachment path; the compact preview adds a “show in composer” action for users who want to edit the pasted text inline.

Normal short text paste behavior is unchanged, and the existing data-URL/image paste path is checked before large text handling so image paste behavior continues to use the current attachment flow.

## User Impact

Users can paste large text into chat without the textarea becoming unwieldy. The pasted text appears as a compact block, can be removed, can be expanded back into the composer, and is still included in the submitted chat payload when left as a block.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts` (`203` tests passed)

  - pasted >2000 characters and verified a compact pasted-text block appeared while the textarea stayed empty
  - removed the pasted-text block
  - pasted again and used “show in composer”; verified the full text returned to the textarea and the block was removed
- Send payload preservation is covered by the focused `handleSendChat` regression test for `text/plain` pasted-text attachments.

target.title: fix(docs): expose top-level docs hubs on mobile
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users browsing the docs site on mobile cannot easily discover or navigate to the desktop top-level docs tabs when the mobile UI collapses the docs navigation.

On desktop, `https://docs.openclaw.ai/` exposes a horizontal top navigation bar with:

`Get started`, `Install`, `Channels`, `Agents`, `Capabilities`, `ClawHub`, `Models`, `Platforms`, `Gateway & Ops`, `Reference`, and `Help`.

On iPhone-sized mobile views, the horizontal top navigation is not visible. The visible mobile `Menu` button opens the current section sidebar only. On the docs home page, that means the user sees the `Get started` section pages (`OpenClaw`, `Showcase`, `Features`, first steps, guides), but not the full desktop tab list. This makes it hard for mobile users to find, or even know about, major docs areas such as `Install`, `Channels`, `Models`, `Platforms`, `Gateway & Ops`, and `Reference`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an early `Browse docs` hub section to the docs home page that mirrors the desktop top-level navigation as normal page content. It does not change the Mintlify navigation configuration or attempt to override Mintlify's mobile menu behavior; it gives mobile users an immediate in-page path to the same top-level docs areas.

## User Impact

Mobile users now get direct, visible links to the major docs areas near the top of the docs home page, even when the mobile menu only exposes the current section sidebar.

## Evidence

Screenshots are kept as PR evidence links instead of product-repo assets. The
links below point to the earlier non-merged fork commit that captured the proof
images; the final PR tree does not add these PNGs.

Desktop docs view: the horizontal top nav is visible and includes the full tab list.

![Desktop docs top navigation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bdjben/openclaw/d1c03771d5596259a289ea36cf90a1458f6f16da/docs/assets/mobile-navigation-evidence/desktop-docs-top-nav.png)

iOS Safari / iPhone 17 Pro Simulator at normal mobile zoom: the desktop horizontal nav is absent from the initial mobile UI. The page shows a `Menu` button, language selector, theme toggle, search, and page content.

![iOS Safari docs home mobile view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bdjben/openclaw/d1c03771d5596259a289ea36cf90a1458f6f16da/docs/assets/mobile-navigation-evidence/ios-safari-docs-home.png)

Mobile-width menu open: the menu opens the current `Get started` sidebar, not the desktop top-level tab list.

![Mobile menu shows current section only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bdjben/openclaw/d1c03771d5596259a289ea36cf90a1458f6f16da/docs/assets/mobile-navigation-evidence/mobile-menu-open.png)

Verification performed:

- Reproduced the live desktop docs UI at `https://docs.openclaw.ai/` with OpenClaw Browser and Puppeteer at `1440x1000`.
- Reproduced the iOS mobile view in the iPhone 17 Pro Simulator running Safari on iOS 26.5.
- Reproduced the opened mobile menu with an iPhone-sized mobile viewport and Safari user agent.
- Confirmed `docs/docs.json` defines the desktop tabs under `navigation.languages[0].tabs`.
- Confirmed the new section links to the same top-level docs areas exposed by the desktop nav.

Checks:

- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` passed locally.
- GitHub Actions `check-docs` passed after refreshing `docs/docs_map.md`.
- GitHub Actions `actionlint`, `no-tabs`, `preflight`, `security-fast`, `security-sensitive-guard`, and `Real behavior proof` passed on the previous clean run.

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): shared search crashes with "search is not a function" when the memory plugin lacks a full search manager
target.body:
Closes #100901

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `wiki search` / `wiki_search` with `search.backend: "shared"` would get `TypeError: sharedMemoryManager.search is not a function` when the active memory plugin registers a search manager that doesn't implement the `MemorySearchManager` contract. `wiki_get` had the same exposure via `manager.readFile`. Concretely hit by `@mem0/openclaw-mem0` ≤ 1.0.14 (plugin-side report: mem0ai/mem0#6113, fix: mem0ai/mem0#6114).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both call sites in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` now check the method exists before calling it and throw an actionable error that names the missing contract method and points at `search.backend: "local"` for wiki-only access. An explicit error was chosen over silently skipping the memory corpus: the user explicitly configured shared search, so silent degradation would hide the misconfiguration. A `manager: null` result keeps its existing graceful handling — this only covers truthy-but-partial managers.

## User Impact

Instead of a bare TypeError from inside the bundle, users get:

```
The active memory plugin's search manager does not implement search() from the MemorySearchManager contract. Set search.backend to "local" for wiki-only access, or use a memory plugin that implements the contract.
```

No behavior change for plugins that implement the contract or report `manager: null`.

## Evidence

- Crash reproduced end-to-end on `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.6.11` in Docker with `@mem0/openclaw-mem0` 1.0.14 (open-source mode, Qdrant): `openclaw wiki search "anything" --backend shared --corpus all` fails with the TypeError above. Full repro in the linked issue.
- After-fix output from this branch (same Docker rig, image built from this branch via the repo Dockerfile, stock `@mem0/openclaw-mem0` 1.0.14). The same command now reports the contract violation instead of the TypeError:

  ```
  $ openclaw wiki search "anything" --backend shared --corpus all
  [openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
  [openclaw] Reason: The active memory plugin's search manager does not implement search() from the
  MemorySearchManager contract. Set search.backend to "local" for wiki-only access, or use a memory
  plugin that implements the contract.
  ```

- New regression tests register a manager with the plugin's exact partial shape: `extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts` ("reports a contract error when the shared manager lacks search()", "reports a contract error when the shared manager lacks readFile()"). Both fail without the fix.
- Local lanes (Windows): `pnpm test:extension memory-wiki` — `query.test.ts` passes 41/41 including the two new tests. The lane's four failures are symlink/hardlink safety tests in `bridge.test.ts`/`okf.test.ts` that fail identically on a clean `main` checkout in this environment (Windows symlink permissions) — untouched by this PR. Repo lint (oxlint shards) passes.

---

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): bridge status crashes on malformed memory-plugin artifacts and ignores readMemoryArtifacts=false
target.body:
Closes #100899

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running memory-wiki in bridge mode with a memory plugin that exports malformed public artifacts would get `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'localeCompare')` from `wiki status` and the `wiki_status` agent tool — and where setting `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts: false` did not stop the agent-tool crash, because the status path never consulted that flag.

Concretely hit by `@mem0/openclaw-mem0` ≤ 1.0.14, which exports record-shaped artifacts with none of the file-backed fields (plugin-side report: mem0ai/mem0#6113, plugin-side fix: mem0ai/mem0#6114). But any plugin can misbehave; the gateway shouldn't crash on bad plugin data.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two small changes:

- `listActiveMemoryPublicArtifacts` now validates plugin-returned artifacts before sorting and drops malformed entries (and non-array listings) with a single warning naming the offending plugin — the same treatment `agentIds` already received in 4644e0c1025. Dropping rather than failing means one bad entry can't take down status for everything else, and the warning makes the plugin bug visible instead of silent.
- `resolveMemoryWikiStatus` now gates artifact enumeration on `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts`, matching the sync path in `bridge.ts` and the CLI's gateway routing, which already honor it. With the flag off, the artifact count reports `null`, consistent with non-bridge modes.

## User Impact

Bridge mode with a misbehaving memory plugin degrades to a logged warning instead of crashing `wiki status` / `wiki_status`, and `readMemoryArtifacts: false` now actually disables artifact enumeration on the status path.

## Evidence

- Crash reproduced end-to-end on `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.6.11` in Docker with `@mem0/openclaw-mem0` 1.0.14 (open-source mode, Qdrant, two stored memories): `openclaw wiki status` and `openclaw gateway call wiki.status` both fail with the `localeCompare` error; with `readMemoryArtifacts: false` the gateway RPC still fails. Full repro in the linked issue. Note the repro needs at least two artifacts — with one, `toSorted` never invokes the comparator, which is easy to false-negative on.
- After-fix output from this branch (same Docker rig, image built from this branch via the repo Dockerfile, stock `@mem0/openclaw-mem0` 1.0.14, same two seeded memories). With `readMemoryArtifacts: true`, both previously-crashing commands now succeed:

  ```
  $ openclaw wiki status
  Wiki vault mode: bridge  Vault: ready (/home/node/.openclaw/wiki/main)  Render mode: native
  Bridge: enabled (0 exported artifacts)  ...
  Warnings: - Bridge mode is enabled but the active memory plugin is not exporting any public memory artifacts yet.

  $ openclaw gateway call wiki.status
  Gateway call: wiki.status
  { "vaultMode": "bridge", ..., "bridge": { "enabled": true, "readMemoryArtifacts": true, ... }, ... }
  ```

  and the gateway log shows the new guard firing instead of the crash:

  ```
  [plugins/memory-state] ignoring 3 malformed public memory artifact(s) from plugin "openclaw-mem0":
  artifacts must include string kind, workspaceDir, relativePath, absolutePath, and contentType
  ```

  (3, not 2 — the plugin derives a third "entity" artifact from the two memories.) With `readMemoryArtifacts: false`, the gateway RPC that previously crashed now returns status with the flag reflected:

  ```
  $ openclaw gateway call wiki.status
  Gateway call: wiki.status
  { "vaultMode": "bridge", ..., "bridge": { "enabled": true, "readMemoryArtifacts": false, ... }, ... }
  ```

- New regression tests use the plugin's exact malformed shape: `src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts` ("drops malformed public memory artifacts instead of crashing the sort", "ignores a non-array public artifact listing") and `extensions/memory-wiki/src/status.test.ts` ("skips artifact enumeration when readMemoryArtifacts is disabled"). All three fail without the fix.
- Local lanes (Windows): `pnpm test:extension memory-wiki` — the touched files pass (`memory-state.test.ts` 17/17, `status.test.ts` 10/10, both including the new tests). The lane's four failures are symlink/hardlink safety tests in `bridge.test.ts`/`okf.test.ts` that fail identically on a clean `main` checkout in this environment (Windows symlink permissions) — untouched by this PR. `pnpm test:contracts:plugins` — one failure (`session-attachments.contract.test.ts`), also identical on clean `main`. `node scripts/check-src-extension-import-boundary.mjs --json` — clean (`[]`). Repo lint (oxlint shards) passes.

---

target.title: fix(gateway): dedupe MCP schema conflict warnings
target.body:
Related: #98437

## What Problem This Solves

Operators see repeated MCP loopback `conflicting schema definitions` warnings every time loopback tool schemas are rebuilt for a different request/session context (`buildMcpToolSchema` runs on every cache miss in `src/gateway/mcp-http.runtime.ts`, and again after the 30s TTL expires). The same field-level first-shape fallback is logged over and over, burying more useful Gateway diagnostics during restart or session churn.

Two further problems in the same code path:

- The warning named only the **field** (`"action"`), not the tool, so it could not be attributed and — worse — deduping on the bare field name meant a genuine, *distinct* conflict on a common field (`action`/`id`/`type`) in a **second, different tool** was silently suppressed by the first tool's warning.
- The structurally identical `malformed schema definition` warning in the same function was left un-deduped and still flooded on every rebuild.

AI-assisted: this PR was prepared with Codex and Claude. I understand the change: it preserves the existing schema-flattening/first-variant behavior and only narrows and attributes duplicate warning emission.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway MCP schema projection already keeps the first schema variant when union object fields conflict. This change keeps that diagnostic signal, but:

- Emits each warning **once per process for a given `(tool, field, reason)`** instead of once per schema rebuild/cache miss.
- Names the tool in the message (`"<tool>.<field>"`) so the warning is attributable and a conflict in one tool no longer suppresses a genuinely different conflict on the same field name in another tool.
- Routes the `malformed schema definition` warning through the same one-per-message helper, fixing the remaining flood.

The dedupe set is keyed on the full message and bounded by the process-stable universe of loopback tool + field names (gateway tool metadata does not change without a restart or explicit reload). The fix stays in the Gateway schema projection layer and does not rename tool fields, change MCP input schemas, or add config.

## User Impact

Operators see far less repeated MCP loopback warning noise while retaining one attributable warning per conflicting/malformed field per tool. Distinct conflicts across different tools are no longer masked. MCP clients continue to receive the same flattened object schema and first-variant precedence as before.

## Evidence

Focused proof run (`src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts` drives the real `buildMcpToolSchema` path across repeated rebuilds and multiple tools):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts

Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  232 passed (232)
```

New regression tests:

- `warns per tool for the same conflicting field name across different tools` — two tools each conflict on `action`; asserts both `mcp_message_send.action` and `mcp_calendar_create.action` warn (fails under the old bare-field-name dedupe, which suppressed the second), and rebuilding twice proves per-`(tool, field)` dedupe survives.
- `warns once per tool for repeated malformed variant schemas across rebuilds` — proves the malformed warning now dedupes instead of flooding.

Additional local checks:

```text
oxfmt --check                 # clean
scripts/run-oxlint.mjs        # clean
tsgo:core + tsgo:core:test    # clean (exit 0)
git diff --check              # clean
```

### Real-runtime live gateway proof (no cloud creds)

Beyond the unit path above, I booted the **real** MCP loopback HTTP server
(`startMcpLoopbackServer`, owner-token auth) and sent `tools/list` over
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` **4x**, each with a distinct `x-openclaw-session-id`
to force 4 genuine `McpLoopbackToolCache` misses -> 4 real `buildMcpToolSchema`
rebuilds (`resolveCallCount === 4`). Tools are injected through the real
`resolveGatewayScopedTools` seam (the same seam plugins feed); the cache, schema
flatten, `warnSchemaOnce`, `logWarn`, and the HTTP handler are all production code.
Captured both log sinks — `logWarn` fan-writes to the terminal `console.log` sink
**and** `getLogger().warn` (the string `"mcp loopback:"` has a space, so it does not
match the subsystem-prefix regex), directly covering the logger double-write concern.

```text
real schema rebuilds forced (cache-miss resolves): 4
tools/list HTTP requests sent: 4

captured warn lines (identical on terminal + structured sinks):
  mcp loopback: conflicting schema definitions for "mcp_message_send.action", keeping the first variant
  mcp loopback: conflicting schema definitions for "mcp_message_send.callId", keeping the first variant
  mcp loopback: conflicting schema definitions for "mcp_calendar_create.action", keeping the first variant
  mcp loopback: malformed schema definition for "mcp_task_run.action", ignoring that variant

(a) mcp_message_send.action conflict    : 1 record/sink across 4 rebuilds (deduped, not 4x)
(b) mcp_task_run.action malformed       : 1 record/sink (no per-rebuild flood)
(c) mcp_calendar_create.action conflict : its own record (per-tool attribution — not
    suppressed by the same-named field in mcp_message_send)
(d) TOTAL: 8 warn records (4 unique x 2 sinks). Without dedupe: 4 warns x 4 rebuilds x 2 sinks = 32.
```

Real loopback server + real HTTP requests; tools injected via the production scoped-tools
seam; both log sinks captured. No cloud creds.

Autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: feat(fs): allow configured workspace aliases
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using `tools.fs.workspaceOnly=true` could not safely keep shared content such as `memory/` outside the per-agent workspace behind an in-workspace symlink. In the layout captured by #90977, memory flushes and file-tool writes to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` failed because the alias resolved outside the workspace even though the operator wanted to allow only that narrow path.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change adds an explicit `tools.fs.workspaceAliases` allowlist so operators can opt in to exact alias roots without weakening the default workspace boundary. The alias path must stay relative to the workspace, the configured target must be an absolute existing directory, the alias realpath must match that target exactly, and direct writes to the target path still reject.

## User Impact

Operators can now keep `workspaceOnly` enabled and still allow a narrow alias such as `memory -> /shared/memory` for read/write/edit plus memory-flush append-only writes. Users do not get broader filesystem access by default, and unconfigured outside-workspace symlink escapes continue to reject.

- Ran a live local runtime proof on the PR branch using the real `createOpenClawCodingTools` path with `tools.fs.workspaceOnly=true` plus `tools.fs.workspaceAliases: [{ path: "memory", target: outsideDir }]`.
- Verified alias-path write/read/edit and memory-triggered append-only writes succeeded through `memory/2026-06-06.md` while direct writes to the outside target path still rejected.
- Added focused regression coverage for config schema handling, alias inheritance/override policy, direct-target rejection, and memory-flush writes through the configured alias.
- Full terminal evidence and focused validation commands remain captured below.

target.title: fix(openai): respect api:"openai-completions" config in transport normalization (#99273)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users setting `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider or per-model level for `openai/*` models were silently ignored. The transport was always forced to `"openai-responses"`, causing every `openai/*` call to hang to idle timeout when the user explicitly configured completions mode.

Previous iterations of this PR only fixed the provider-level path. This iteration adds per-model detection — when `api: "openai-completions"` is set on a specific model row (e.g. `models.providers.openai.models: [{id: "gpt-5.5", api: "openai-completions"}]`), it is now also respected.

Fixes #99273.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two independently incorrect things were happening:

1. **`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`** had a single-char logic bug (`!==` vs `===`) that forced explicit completions config to Responses.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport`** shared the same predicate with the transport callback, but models that reach the resolved-model path carry `api: "openai-completions"` as a catalog default — the resolved model's `api` field does not carry provenance. So per-model user config like `{id: "gpt-5.5", api: "openai-completions"}` was indistinguishable from the catalog default `"openai-completions"` after resolution.

The fix has four parts:

1. **`hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig()`** — New helper that checks BOTH `config.models.providers.openai.api` (provider-level) and `config.models.providers.openai.models[].api` (per-model level) to distinguish user intent from catalog defaults.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport()`** — Rewritten with its own catalog-normalization logic (checks owner provider + default baseUrl + default api), decoupled from `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`.

3. **`normalizeResolvedModel` callback** — Checks `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` before calling `normalizeOpenAITransport`. When the user explicitly configured completions at either level, returns the model unchanged.

4. **`normalizeTransport` callback** — Checks `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` before calling `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`. When the user explicitly configured completions, returns `undefined` (no override).

**Not modified**: Codex Responses transport hooks, auth profiles, usage tracking, live catalog fetching.

## User Impact

Users who explicitly configure `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider level OR on a specific model row now have their configuration respected. Default behavior for catalog OpenAI models (normalize to Responses) is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Production-code proof — all 3 config levels

Proof script imports the real `buildOpenAIProvider()` and exercises both `normalizeResolvedModel` and `normalizeTransport` callbacks against catalog-default, provider-level, and per-model config scenarios:

```
$ npx tsx scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs

[PASS] resolved: catalog → Responses
[PASS] resolved: provider-level explicit completions  
[PASS] resolved: per-model explicit completions        ← THE FIX (was broken)
[PASS] transport: catalog → Responses
[PASS] transport: provider explicit → undefined
[PASS] transport: per-model explicit → undefined        ← THE FIX (was broken)

6/6 passed
```

### Data flow proof — per-model config survives normalization

```
User config:  {openai: {models: [{id: "gpt-5.5", api: "openai-completions"}]}}
  ↓ model.ts:747-757
  metadataOverrideModel.api = "openai-completions"      (per-model wins)
  resolvedModel.api = "openai-completions"
  ↓ normalizeResolvedModel callback
  hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig(config, "gpt-5.5")
    → openaiCfg.models.some(m => m.id === "gpt-5.5" && m.api === "openai-completions")
    → TRUE → return ctx.model unchanged ✅
```

### Test regression

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)

$ npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts --run
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  246 passed (246)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts
→ exit 0
```

### What was not tested

| Not tested | Why acceptable |
|------------|----------------|
| Real OpenAI endpoint E2E for each config level | The proof exercises the exact `normalizeResolvedModel` and `normalizeTransport` callback functions with their real production implementations — the same functions the gateway calls. Whether the API key works beyond this transport-normalization boundary is a separate concern from this predicate fix. |

## Root Cause

Two coupled problems in `extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts`:

1. **`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`**: A single-character logic error (`!==` for `===`) at L462 caused the early-return guard to execute the opposite of its intended behavior. But fixing this alone broke the transport path's catalog normalization.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport`**: Shared the same predicate, creating a coupling where the resolved-model path's catalog normalization and the transport path's per-request override used the same boolean function. After model resolution, the resolved `api` field carries no provenance bit — a per-model `api: "openai-completions"` config and the catalog default `api: "openai-completions"` are identical strings. The only way to distinguish them is to inspect the raw config.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Claude Opus 4.8 (Anthropic). The author understands and takes responsibility for all code changes.

target.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_yield` without a continuation source silently parks an interactive direct session — the turn completes with `yieldDetected: true` and zero payloads, so the user sees nothing and the bot appears hung. This adds a diagnostic payload when the yielded turn has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, async tools, or cron adds, so the user gets a visible message instead of a silent hang.

- **Problem**: `run.ts` always returns no payloads when `yieldDetected=true`, even when no continuation source exists. The incomplete-turn fallback is suppressed by the yield flag, so no visible output reaches the user.
- **Solution**: Extract a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` helper in `incomplete-turn.ts` (the continuation subset of `hasAttemptTerminalState` minus self-reference, plus `countActiveDescendantRuns`), then call it from `run.ts` to check for concrete continuation evidence before trusting a yield as terminal. When payloads are empty and `yieldDetected` has no continuation sources, emit a diagnostic text payload.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts` — new exported `hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt, activeDescendantCount?)` + `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant, placed next to sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` — inline predicate replaced with shared helper call; triple-nested ternary uses shared constant
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — 4 new tests: 3 diagnostic-suppression (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) + 1 async-tool purity
- **What did NOT change**: Yield acceptance semantics, `hasAttemptTerminalState`, `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`, liveness state classification. No existing yield path is altered.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #100065
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a model calls `sessions_yield` before establishing any continuation (before spawning subagents, sending messages, starting async tools, or scheduling cron work), the runtime accepts the yield unconditionally. The turn records `yieldDetected: true` with no payloads, liveness becomes `"paused"`, and the session produces no visible output. From the user's perspective the bot simply stops responding — no error, no fallback, no diagnostic.

The yield tool's own contract says "Use **after** spawning subagents; results arrive as next message." A yield before spawning violates this contract, but the runtime has no guard. This fix adds a user-visible signal so the silent park is replaced with a diagnostic message.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: `sessions_yield` without continuation evidence no longer returns empty payloads silently. A diagnostic text is emitted.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, fix/yield-no-continuation-diagnostic-100065 branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Live proof: shared hasYieldContinuationEvidence logic (7 scenarios)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { hasYieldContinuationEvidence } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts";

function shouldEmitDiagnostic(attempt) {
  const hasContinuation = attempt.yieldDetected && hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt);
  if (attempt.yieldDetected && !hasContinuation)
    return { diagnostic: true, text: "⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume." };
  return { diagnostic: false };
}

const cases = [
  ["bare yield, no continuation", { yieldDetected: true }],
  ["yield + accepted spawn", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [{ runId: "c", childSessionKey: "k" }] }],
  ["yield + committed delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["answer"] }],
  ["yield + whitespace delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["   "] }],
  ["yield + empty spawn array", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [] }],
  ["yield + async tool in flight", { yieldDetected: true, toolMetas: [{ asyncStarted: true }] }],
  ["yield + approval prompt", { yieldDetected: true, didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt: true }],
];
for (const [name, att] of cases)
  console.log(`${shouldEmitDiagnostic(att).diagnostic ? "DIAGNOSTIC" : "SILENT    "} — ${name}`);
NODE

# 2. Regression test suite (121 tests)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \

$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'

SILENT     — yield + accepted spawn

```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 121 yield/incomplete-turn tests pass — no regression. Four new tests cover: (a) bare yield with no continuation → diagnostic emitted, (b) whitespace-only delivery text → NOT counted as continuation, (c) empty spawn array → NOT counted as continuation, (d) three suppression scenarios (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) → diagnostic suppressed.
  2. The change is purely additive: when a yield has continuation evidence (spawns, delivery, async tools, cron, or active descendant runs), behavior is identical to before.
  3. When a yield has no continuation evidence, a diagnostic payload `"⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume."` is emitted instead of an empty payload array.
  4. Normalized helpers (`hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, `hasCommittedMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`) correctly reject whitespace-only delivery text and empty spawn arrays — preventing false continuation signals.
  5. `countActiveDescendantRuns()` is safely imported and returns 0 when no active descendants exist, preserving the diagnostic for bare yields while correctly skipping it when the session has in-flight child work.

- **What was not tested**: Live Telegram/Discord environment (no bot tokens available). The gateway run used a local ZTE provider (Qwen3-235B-A22B), not a Telegram/Discord channel. The core diagnostic path (yield without continuation → user-visible message) is proven identical across all channels since it runs at the embedded-runner layer.

## Root Cause

Three compounding gaps allow the silent park:

1. **`sessions-yield-tool.ts`** — No validation at the tool level. Accepts any yield regardless of continuation state.
2. **`incomplete-turn.ts:261`** — `yieldDetected` causes `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText` to return `null` immediately, suppressing the incomplete-turn fallback.
3. **`run.ts:4125-4148`** — The yield-specific path always returns no payloads, regardless of whether continuation evidence exists.

This PR addresses (3) only — it is the safest additive fix. A deeper fix for (1) would require a product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a model calls `sessions_yield` without establishing any continuation source, the user now sees a diagnostic message instead of a silent hang. No change for legitimate yield patterns (those with accepted spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron adds).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No. The new test file (`sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts`) is additive — it does not modify existing serialized state or snapshots, requires no migration or upgrade path.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, for the current scope. This is a narrow additive change that fixes the UX gap (silent hang → visible diagnostic) without requiring a product decision on continuation semantics.
- **Refactor needed**: Yes — the reviewer in #100146 identified that the initial inline predicate was a fourth copy of the continuation logic that would drift. The fix extracts a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` in `incomplete-turn.ts`, reuses `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity`, and places the `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant next to its sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`. `run.ts` is now orchestration-only for this path.
- **Alternative considered**: A deeper fix at the tool level (`sessions-yield-tool.ts`) that rejects yields without continuation evidence. This would be more correct but needs a product decision on what counts as a valid continuation source, maintainer agreement on guard semantics, and plumbing of subscribe-handler state into the tool layer. Marked as future work.

### Future work (Step 2)

A follow-up PR could validate continuation sources inside `sessions_yield` tool execution and reject a yield that has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, or async work. This requires:
- Access to subscribe-handler state from the tool layer
- A product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source
- Tests for the rejection path

The diagnostic signal from this PR creates the contract surface for that future enforcement. The active-descendant check (`countActiveDescendantRuns`) already handles the most common existing-wake scenario.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None. The change is purely additive — it only activates when `yieldDetected=true` AND payloads are empty AND no continuation evidence exists. All existing yield patterns (with spawns, delivery, async tools, cron) continue unchanged.
- **Mitigations**: The continuation check uses the same fields already tracked for `hasAttemptTerminalState`; no new state or tracing is introduced. Suppression tests (accepted spawn / async tool / active descendant run) guard against always-false regression in the shared helper.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. Deploying this change has no effect on sessions with legitimate yield patterns.

target.title: fix(config): preserve empty env var values in config resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes two related issues where `resolveConfigValue` / `resolveConfigValueUncached` use `||` (boolean OR) instead of `??` (nullish coalescing), causing an explicitly-set empty environment variable to fall through to the literal config key name.

**Bug 1 — resolver fallback semantics**: When `MY_API_KEY=""`, the `||` operator treats empty string as falsy and returns the literal `"MY_API_KEY"` as the API credential. This produces a confusing "invalid API key" error from the provider instead of a clear "not configured" failure.

**Bug 2 — auth status / availability disagreement**: `ModelRegistry.getProviderAuthStatus` and `hasConfiguredAuth` disagreed about empty env-backed API keys. `getProviderAuthStatus` treated empty env vars as configured, while `hasConfiguredAuth` returned true for any provider with an `apiKey` field, so model availability, restore, and selection could still route to a provider whose status said it was unconfigured.

## Why This Change Was Made
- Replaced `||` with `??` in both `resolveConfigValue` and `resolveConfigValueUncached` so that an explicitly-set empty environment variable is preserved rather than silently reinterpreted as a literal config string.
- Updated `getProviderAuthStatus` to use `in` operator to distinguish "env var set to empty" from "env var not set", and return `configured: false` when the env var is explicitly empty.
- Updated `hasConfiguredAuth` / `getAvailable` to reject only explicitly empty env-backed `apiKey` values while preserving `AuthStorage.hasAuth` semantics (stored auth, runtime `--api-key` overrides, env-key discovery, fallback resolver) and the AWS SDK sentinel path.
- Added regression coverage for resolver, auth status, `getApiKeyAndHeaders`, availability, and runtime override paths.

## User Impact
Users who accidentally leave an API key env var set to empty will now get a consistent "API key not configured" signal across status, model availability, and runtime requests instead of a confusing "invalid API key" error from their provider. Runtime `--api-key` overrides continue to make models available.

## Evidence

### Full-chain proof (current HEAD)
Real environment: Linux x86_64, Node 22.22. Proof drives production `resolveConfigValue`, `ModelRegistry`, and `AuthStorage` through a temporary `models.json` file on disk — no mocks of tested functions.

```

ok: ?? returns empty string
ok: ?? uncached returns empty string

[case 2] resolveConfigValue: env var set to real key
ok: real env value returned
ok: real env value returned uncached

[case 3] resolveConfigValue: env var not set (literal fallback)
ok: missing env falls back to literal key name
ok: missing env falls back to literal key name uncached

[case 4] ModelRegistry.getProviderAuthStatus: empty env-backed apiKey
ok: empty env -> configured: false - {"configured":false}

[case 5] ModelRegistry.getApiKeyAndHeaders: empty env-backed apiKey
ok: getApiKeyAndHeaders returns ok:false - {"ok":false,"error":"No API key found for \"openclaw-proof-provider\""}

[case 6] ModelRegistry.getAvailable/hasConfiguredAuth: empty env-backed apiKey
ok: getAvailable excludes empty-env provider
ok: hasConfiguredAuth returns false

[case 7] ModelRegistry availability with runtime API key override + empty env
ok: runtime override keeps provider available despite empty env
ok: hasConfiguredAuth returns true with runtime override
ok: getApiKeyAndHeaders uses runtime override - {"ok":true,"apiKey":"sk-runtime-override"}

[case 8] ModelRegistry.getProviderAuthStatus: real env-backed apiKey
ok: real env -> configured: true, source: environment - {"configured":true,"source":"environment","label":"OPENCLAW_PROOF_REAL_KEY"}

[case 9] ModelRegistry.getAvailable/hasConfiguredAuth: real env-backed apiKey
ok: getAvailable includes real-env provider
ok: hasConfiguredAuth returns true

[case 10] ModelRegistry.getProviderAuthStatus: missing env (literal fallback)
ok: missing env -> configured: true, source: models_json_key - {"configured":true,"source":"models_json_key"}

[case 11] ModelRegistry.getAvailable/hasConfiguredAuth: missing env (literal fallback)
ok: getAvailable includes literal-key provider
ok: hasConfiguredAuth returns true

[case 12] ModelRegistry.getProviderAuthStatus: shell command apiKey
ok: shell command -> configured: true, source: models_json_command - {"configured":true,"source":"models_json_command"}

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip heartbeat when session idle too long, back off after consecutive idle skips
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Heartbeat continues firing against a long-idle session with no user to receive output, burning expensive API tokens until the account spend cap intervenes. A heartbeat on an idle session wastes money because there's no user context to act on and no one to receive the result.

- **Problem**: `runHeartbeatOnce()` has no awareness of session staleness. It fires on a fixed interval (default 30min) regardless of whether the session has had human interaction in days or weeks. In the reported case (#98556), a single idle session consumed ~$168 in 5 days before the spend cap hit; the family chain burned ~$248 total. Even `/reset` didn't stop it — the new session inherited the same agent key and heartbeats resumed immediately.
- **Solution**: Gate the heartbeat on the resolved session's last real interaction time. If the last user/channel interaction is older than 7 days, skip the heartbeat. Additionally, track consecutive idle skips per agent and escalate to a backoff skip after 48 consecutive idle heartbeats (~1 day at 30min interval), handling edge cases like `/reset` creating fresh sessions.
- **What changed**: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` (~40 lines of runtime logic), `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.test-utils.ts` (extended `HeartbeatSessionSeed` type), new `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts` (7 test cases).
- **What did NOT change**: No new config keys, types, schema, or public API. No changes to `heartbeat-wake.ts`, `heartbeat-schedule.ts`, or the scheduler layer. No behavioral change for active sessions.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #98556
- Related to #14051
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression (partial fix for the zombie-session spend scenario; #14051 remains open for the full configurable idle-timeout feature)

## Motivation

Issue #98556 reports a production incident where a `main` session idle for 21 days silently consumed ~$248 in Anthropic Opus 4.7 spend through heartbeat polls that fired every 30 minutes. The heartbeat runner had no awareness of session staleness — it checked HEARTBEAT.md content, active hours, queue busyness, and preflight conditions, but never consulted `lastInteractionAt` or any session freshness signal.

This is a runtime safety guard, not a product feature. It uses a hardcoded 7-day threshold (not a new config key) so users without any idle policy are still protected. Issue #14051 tracks the broader product decision for a configurable activity-based idle timeout; this fix provides a safety baseline until that feature lands.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Heartbeats should not fire on sessions that have been idle longer than 7 days, because there is no user to receive output and no new context for the agent to act on.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 22, branch `fix/heartbeat-idle-gate-98556`, based on `origin/main` HEAD.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  1. Ran 7 unit tests for the idle gate + 13 existing commitment tests (zero regression).
  2. Ran a standalone proof script that calls `runHeartbeatOnce()` directly via `node --import tsx`, seeding a real session store with controlled `lastInteractionAt` values.

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```console
  $ node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-98556-evidence/proof.mts

  === Heartbeat Idle Gate: Real Runtime Proof ===

  [1/3] Active session (1 min idle)
        status: ran

  [2/3] Idle session (8 days idle)
        status: skipped, reason: session-idle

  [3/3] Fallback (sessionStartedAt 8 days ago, no lastInteractionAt)
        status: skipped, reason: session-idle

  === All tests passed ===
  ```

  | Test case | Input | Expected | Result |
  |-----------|-------|----------|--------|
  | Active session | `lastInteractionAt = 1 min ago` | `status: "ran"` | ✅ `ran` |
  | Idle 8 days | `lastInteractionAt = 8 days ago` | `status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle"` | ✅ `skipped / session-idle` |
  | No lastInteractionAt | `sessionStartedAt = 8 days ago` | `status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle"` | ✅ `skipped / session-idle` |
  | Unit: exactly at threshold | `lastInteractionAt = 7d+1ms ago` | skip | ✅ |
  | Unit: only updatedAt | `updatedAt = 7d+1m ago` | skip | ✅ |
  | Unit: recent sessionStartedAt | `sessionStartedAt = 1 min ago` | ran | ✅ |
  | Unit: no entry | no seed data | ran (no-op) | ✅ |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. Sessions with `lastInteractionAt` older than 7 days: heartbeat skipped with `reason: "session-idle"`.
  2. After 48 consecutive idle skips per agent: escalated to `reason: "backoff-idle"`.
  3. Sessions with recent `lastInteractionAt`: no behavioral change — heartbeat runs normally.
  4. Sessions with no `lastInteractionAt`: falls back to `sessionStartedAt`, then `updatedAt`.
  5. Sessions with no entry at all: idle gate is a no-op, execution continues to existing preflight checks.
- **What was not tested**: Live gateway soak with a real 7-day idle session (impractical in unit test); the consecutive backoff counter persistence across gateway restarts (in-memory Map, resets on restart by design).

## Root Cause

The heartbeat runner (`runHeartbeatOnce()` in `heartbeat-runner.ts:1395`) performs 13 skip checks (disabled, quiet-hours, queue busy, cron in progress, active reply runs, lane busy, pending delivery, empty HEARTBEAT.md, etc.) but never consults the resolved session's interaction staleness. The `lastInteractionAt` field has existed on `SessionEntry` since inception and is correctly preserved (not updated) by heartbeat runs — it was simply never read by the heartbeat scheduler.

This is a design omission, not a regression: the runner was built without session-activity awareness.

```
Provenance: carried forward since heartbeat runner creation — never introduced
by a specific commit, never fixed.
Confidence: clear
```

## Regression Test Plan

7 new unit tests cover the idle gate behavior. 13 existing commitment tests confirm zero regression. The change is local to `runHeartbeatOnce()` and does not touch the scheduler, wake layer, delivery path, or any public API.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with sessions idle longer than 7 days will see heartbeats automatically skipped (logged as `"session-idle"`) with no action required. Active sessions are unaffected. No new configuration or user intervention needed.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Reproduction + Verification

### Environment (unit test)
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Runtime/container: Node.js 22

### Steps (unit test)
1. Seed session store with `lastInteractionAt` set to more than 7 days ago.
2. Call `runHeartbeatOnce()` with `target: "none"`.
3. Observe `{ status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle" }`.

### Expected
Heartbeat skips on idle sessions, runs normally on active sessions.

### Actual (before fix)
Heartbeat runs regardless of session staleness.

## Evidence Checklist

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets (unit test output)
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: 7 test cases covering idle/active/no-entry/fallback chains; 13 existing commitment tests for regression.
- **Edge cases checked**: `lastInteractionAt` undefined, `sessionStartedAt` undefined, both undefined (only `updatedAt` available), no session entry at all.
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway with real 7-day idle session (logistically impractical); the consecutive backoff counter persisting across gateway restarts (by design it's an in-memory Map).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds a new skip path for sessions past the idle threshold; all other paths unchanged.
- [x] Config/env changes? No — no new config keys, env vars, or schema changes.
- [x] Migration needed? No.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The idle gate addresses the root cause (no staleness awareness) at the right boundary (inside `runHeartbeatOnce()`, where the session entry is already resolved and all other skip conditions are checked). The 7-day threshold is a hardcoded safety net that requires no product decision; Issue #14051 remains open for the configurable feature.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**:
  1. Adding a new config key `heartbeat.idleTimeoutMinutes` — rejected because CLAUDE.md policy sets a high bar for new config surface, and the product decision belongs to #14051.
  2. Hooking into `evaluateSessionFreshness()` — rejected because the session's `idleMinutes` policy is about session reset, not heartbeat cost protection, and may be unconfigured.
  3. Agent-level spend circuit breaker — more comprehensive but requires cross-session accounting and new state; overkill for this fix.

## Relationship to #14051

Issue #14051 proposes a configurable activity-based heartbeat idle timeout (`heartbeat.idleTimeoutMinutes`). That feature requires a product decision (config name, schema, default behavior) and is tracked separately. This PR does **not** implement #14051. Instead, it provides a hardcoded runtime safety guard that prevents runaway cost while the #14051 product decision is pending. When #14051 is eventually implemented, its configurable threshold would naturally replace the 7-day hardcoded fallback for users who set it.

ClawSweeper's most recent review (2026-07-06) on #14051 lists "Keep existing primitives only" as an option and notes that this is a maintainer product decision; this PR's no-new-config approach aligns with the conservative end of that spectrum.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Users with legitimate heartbeat tasks that fire less often than every 7 days (e.g., a weekly heartbeat report).  
**Mitigation**: The 7-day threshold is long enough that any reasonable periodic task (daily check-in, monitoring, etc.) will fire well within the window. A weekly report would fire on day 0 (fresh session) and day 7 would be exactly at the boundary — the test covers this edge case.  
**Compatibility impact**: None for active sessions. The only sessions affected are those with no human interaction for >7 days, which are precisely the sessions that should not be heartbeating.  
**Backoff escalation risk**: The 48-consecutive-skip backoff is purely in-memory (agent-level Map) and resets on restart, so a misconfigured system can recover after a restart without operator action.

---

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Human confirmed understanding of code changes: Yes

Related to #98556
Related to #14051

target.title: fix: A2A handoffs can duplicate message-tool replies
target.body:
Related: #39476
Related: #91161
Related: #93293

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users asking an agent to hand work to another session could receive duplicate visible output when the target session replied through `message(action="send")` and the waited A2A path later treated transcript bookkeeping as a fresh assistant reply.

This PR was triggered by a real local WhatsApp/Main Merid duplicate-delivery report. The private message content is intentionally not included, but the observed shape was: one correct requester-visible reply, followed by a second visible message derived from the same A2A/source-reply flow.

This is a narrow companion to #39476. It does not replace #91161's reverse `sessions_send` tool guard, and it does not change compaction replay behavior covered by #93293.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps waited A2A reply extraction on model-authored assistant replies instead of transcript artifacts. It excludes inter-session input rows, raw OpenClaw delivery mirrors, projected message-tool mirrors, and Gateway-injected assistant rows before they can feed ping-pong or announce delivery.

It also keeps same-session A2A source replies from re-running the announce decider when there is no valid announce target, and treats incomplete-turn fallback text as non-deliverable in the A2A announce path.

No production config, secrets, channel adapter contract, tool schema, delivery API, runtime permission, package metadata, or changelog file is changed.

## User Impact

A2A handoffs that reply visibly through the message tool no longer turn already-delivered source replies or forwarded `sessions_send` transcript rows into a second visible message. Normal model-authored assistant replies still use the existing waited reply, ping-pong, and announce behavior.

## Evidence

Current-head proof after rebasing onto `upstream/main` `5aa7c6267cc0`; pushed PR head `97d3b936fd`. Latest checked upstream movement was IRC-only and did not touch this PR's files; the rebased branch merges cleanly.

target.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets
target.body:
## Summary

ws 8.21.0 introduced `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` receiver limits (commit `[security] Limit retained message parts`) that can trigger `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and close connections with code 1008 under certain traffic patterns.

This PR explicitly sets both limits to `0` (disabled) for Discord gateway WebSocket connections, restoring the ws 8.20.0 behavior for the trusted Discord gateway peer while preserving the security fix for all other WebSocket usage.

## Changes

- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`**: Base class `createWebSocket()` now passes `maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0` with a `ws.ClientOptions` cast (since `@types/ws` 8.18.1 does not yet expose these fields).
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`**: Extended `DiscordGatewayWebSocketCtor` type to include the new options; monitor gateway creation path passes the same disabled limits.
- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`**: Added test verifying base class WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts`**: Added test verifying monitor plugin WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.proxy.test.ts`**: Updated two existing exact-match assertions to include the new options.

## Why `0` instead of raising the limits

- ws 8.21.0 treats `0` as disabled (`receiver.js:61`, `receiver.js:98`: `if (this._maxBufferedChunks > 0 && ...)`), matching the pre-8.21.0 behavior exactly.
- Discord gateway is a trusted peer; the security limits are designed to protect against untrusted senders.
- Choosing an arbitrary higher threshold would be fragile without real production traffic data to calibrate against.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: ws 8.21.0's retained-part receiver limits (`maxFragments` default 131072 / `maxBufferedChunks` default 1048576) abort a Discord gateway socket with `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` / close `1008`; this PR sets both to `0` (disabled) on the Discord gateway sockets, restoring ws 8.20.0 behavior for that trusted peer.
- **Real environment tested**: Live Discord gateway connection from a Docker `node:22-bookworm-slim` container (Node `v22.22.3`) with the repo-pinned `ws@8.21.0` installed exactly, using a real bot token (redacted), connecting to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: build a `node:22-bookworm-slim` image with `npm install ws@8.21.0`, then run a client that constructs the gateway socket with this patch's options (`new ws.WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 30000, maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0 })`), completes the HELLO/IDENTIFY/READY handshake against the real Discord gateway, sends heartbeats, holds a 60s stable window, then closes with code 1000.
- **Evidence after fix**: Live Discord gateway run with this patch's options applied (token, `session_id`, and `resume_gateway_url` redacted):

```
[env] node=v22.22.3 ws=8.21.0
[discord] connecting wss://gateway.discord.gg (maxBufferedChunks:0, maxFragments:0)
[discord] open
[discord] HELLO heartbeat_interval=41250ms
[discord] IDENTIFY sent (token redacted)
[discord] READY received (session_id/resume_gateway_url redacted)
[discord] HEARTBEAT_ACK #1
[discord] stable window 60000ms complete
[discord] close code=1000 reason=<empty>
[result] PASS live: READY + 1 heartbeat ACK; no WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS during stable window
```

Supplemental deterministic mechanism repro against a local ws 8.21.0 gateway streaming one message in 131073 fragments (one over the client default `maxFragments`), exercising the same `ws.WebSocket` receiver path:

```
# default ws.WebSocket (ws 8.21 defaults)
[before] open
[before] error code=WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS message=Too many message fragments
[before] close code=1006 reason=<empty>

# this patch's options applied
[after] open
[after] message received: 131073 bytes - NO receiver-limit close
```

- **Observed result after fix**: On the real Discord gateway, with the disabled limits applied, the connection reaches `READY`, exchanges heartbeats, and stays connected through the 60s window with no `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and no `1008` close; the only close is the intentional client-initiated `1000`. The deterministic repro confirms the same constructor options remove the receiver-limit close that the default ws 8.21 client hits.
- **What was not tested**: the live run confirms a real gateway session stays healthy with the patched options, but does not force Discord's production fragmentation pattern on demand, does not exercise the `zlib-stream` transport, and does not drive the full OpenClaw plugin wiring end-to-end. The deterministic repro proves the ws 8.21 retained-part mechanism and that this patch's options disable the exact receiver checks, but uses a local peer rather than Discord's live framing.

## Tests

- `gateway.test.ts`: 25 passed
- `gateway-plugin.test.ts`: 17 passed  
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: 21 passed
- TypeScript check (tsgo): clean

Fixes #88330

target.title: fix(media): map sandbox media with active workdir
target.body:
Closes #98446

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenShell sandbox users could generate media under `/sandbox/...` but reply/message media handling only recognized `/workspace/...`, causing sandbox media transfer to be rejected before outbound delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix threads the active sandbox `containerWorkdir` into sandbox media normalization and outbound message-action media policy. It keeps `/workspace` as the default for Docker-style sandboxes, normalizes trailing slash spellings such as `/sandbox/`, and does not loosen OpenShell managed-root validation.

## User Impact

OpenShell sandbox media paths under `/sandbox/...` can now resolve to the host sandbox workspace for reply and message-action delivery. Docker `/workspace/...` behavior is unchanged, and similarly named paths such as `/sandboxer/...` remain rejected.

## Evidence

Head SHA: d272cf5ef95dac88d3da48d4d3b2a803704a3e9d

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 23 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox-paths.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-action-params.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.media.test.ts src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts` passed: 4 files, 208 passed / 13 skipped.
- Real OpenShell backend proof passed on the contributor fork at the same head: https://github.com/qingminglong/openclaw/actions/runs/28793386124

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Linked plugin path: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],

  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",

      "vision_map.describe_workflow",
      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",
      "vision_map.type_text",
      "vision_map.press_key",
      "vision_map.scroll",
      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.
